For instance, when introducing Yuri to Loid, Yuri asked her why she neglected to tell him that not only had she gotten married, but that she had supposedly been married for an entire year. Loid had privately suggested to Yor that she simply tell Yuri the truth about their marriage of convenience, but Yor convinced him that she had a better idea. However, instead of suggesting something generally plausible, Yor simply told Yuri that she had forgotten to tell him. When pressed further, she elaborated that not only had she forgotten, but she then forgot that she had forgotten. While it mildly exasperated Yuri and flabbergasted Loid to a degree, Yuri did not question her answer as such a thing was completely in character for her.

Yor's unintentional displays of physical prowess around Loid and Anya have prompted a number of ridiculous excuses on her part. In one instance she claimed to have learned about pressure points capable of paralyzing a rampaging cow through a yoga class, and in another, she attempted to explain away her strength as a consequence of having once apprenticed as a blacksmith. Loid, likely due to his own exceedingly abnormal perspective, apparently has yet to take issue with any of these explanations, while Anya is of course aware of the truth due to her powers.

Lack of Conventional Education: Because Yor has been working as an assassin since she was a child, she appears to have not learned much from school to the point that Yuri would be teaching her more than she did when they studied. Despite this, Yor has enough basic literacy, typing, and organization skills to maintain a job as a clerk at city hall. She is also completely functional as an adult in the society in which she lives, and she successfully cared for her brother, alone, from the time he was a small child into adulthood. However, she once revealed that she had no idea what the term "First Lady" meant, and once when trying to solve a math problem on Anya's homework, she became distracted by imagining a gingerbread man being dismembered and failed to do so.

Insecurities: Yor's biggest weakness is her low self-esteem. Because of this, she is very insecure about herself and is often seen believing Loid is disappointed with her and feels unfit to be a wife and a mother. This makes her prone to imagining situations that are far from reality and misinterpret things, such as thinking that Loid was having an affair with Fiona, his co-worker, and would get replaced by her. Much later, Yuri suggested to her that Loid was having an affair after he suddenly rushed off to deal with an emergency. Despite not believing that to be the case, the mere possibility was upsetting enough to distract her for the remainder of the day.

Perhaps her single greatest insecurity, however, is her feelings of general abnormality. She seems to have absolutely no idea what "normal" people do or why, which leads her to have significantly overblown concerns about not sticking out. It also often results in her catastrophizing entirely benign situations. For instance, she once parkoured all the way to Anya's school to deliver her P.E. uniform, as she thought that if Anya did not have it, she would be expelled. Not only was that not the case, but Anya had deliberately left the uniform at home as she did not have P.E. that day.

Both Loid and Anya have helped Yor to begin working past her insecurities as they affirm her as part of their family, with Anya saying that she likes the way Yor already is, while Loid has praised her abilities as a mother on multiple occasions and told Yor that he does not intend to replace her with Fiona.

(To Vice Minister Brennan): "I apologize for the intrusion, but... may I have the honor of taking your life?"
(To herself, referring to Anya): "I know that this family is just for appearances. But… I still feel like… I want to be a better mother to that girl… Maybe I'll never be like a normal mother, but I'll do my best with what I've got!"
(Regarding the Forger family): "It was a surprise to me too. The only attachment I've ever had was to my brother. I never imagined I'd find a place like this, that I was so unwilling to leave behind."
(To the Assassin Leader): "Yes, I killed them. Why wouldn't I? When you point a blade at someone, you don't get to complain when one is pointed back at you. Same goes for me."
(To herself, remembering her family): "The world is soiled with needless tragedies. To prevent just one of them from befalling him or anyone else… takes thorough cleaning. And that still hasn't changed. In fact… now it's more true than ever."
(To Loid): "I know that you can do pretty much anything by yourself. And when times are hard for you, you try to spare me from it. But I don't think you need to be so perfect all the time. So when you actually asked me for help just now, it made me kind of happy."
(To herself): "My parents are gone, and Loid's are too. So Anya's never experienced having a grandparent before. I guess I never have either, but... You can't miss what you've never known, so I can't say I was ever sad about that. But I wonder if that's true for Anya as well?"

entries.name: Bond Forger
entries.content:
“You did a great job today. That was impressive. That said… you have to be more careful. Because there is someone else back home who'd be heartbroken if anything happened to you. I'm sorry about before, your working duties should always come second. I want you to think of yourself as a member of the Forger Family, first and foremost.”
— Loid Forger to Bond

Bond Forger (ボンド・フォージャー, Bondo Fōjā?) is one of the main characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. He is the pet dog of the Forger Family. Formerly known as Subject 8 (実験体8号, Jikkentai Hachi-gō?, lit. "Experimental Subject No. 8"), Bond was used as a test subject in the Ostanian research project known as Project Apple, which resulted in him gaining precognitive abilities.

Bond is a large dog of an indeterminate breed with fluffy white fur and black paws, noted by Anya to resemble the gloves and shoes of Bondman. His large stature, long coat, color, and the shape of his snout suggest he is mostly Great Pyrenees, and he is large enough for Anya Forger to comfortably ride on. Bond's eyes are small and dark, and he has small ears that usually droop down. When his fur is wet, his body is revealed to be much thinner than his fur suggests, and for some reason, it also affects his bark.

Bond usually wears a collar in the style of a bow tie, given to him by Anya after she came up with his name.

Despite his dark background, Bond is shown to be a very kind dog, as he uses his precognition abilities to help others who find themselves in danger in his visions, from rescuing a child from being hit by a falling board to assisting Anya in preventing the death of Loid Forger. He also helps Anya to retrieve her favorite pair of gloves from a fierce dog by intimidating him. However, he is also shown to be overzealous and quick to seek gratification, often resulting in him acting prematurely and causing the misfortunes he tries to prevent.

Bond is also shown to have a petty and jealous streak, destroying Anya's beloved stuffed penguin when he felt it was getting more attention from Anya than himself. He did apologize to Anya, however, by fetching her a bag of peanuts after seeing how badly this act had upset her. While they did make up afterward, Bond continues to be jealous whenever Anya gets a new toy that she shows off to the rest of the family.

Due in part to his past as a lab rat and the abuse he suffered in Project Apple, Bond is somewhat unnerved by dog training techniques. The amount of time he spent there was so long that he was initially unfamiliar with the simple act of playing, as he remained mostly stationary during his first trip to the dog park. After being taken in by the Forger family, Bond has gained a comfortable life filled with love and care, which he reciprocates in his desire to protect the family.

Bond's time as a research experiment left him with precognitive abilities and above-average intelligence for a dog. He is capable of understanding human speech.

Precognition: Bond gained precognitive abilities from the experiments done to him, allowing him to briefly see sometimes fragmented scenes from a few minutes to a few hours into the future. These visions are shown from Bond's perspective, taking the form of an old television screen with static noises, and he is even able to hear what happens in these moments. This power is indicated to be active whenever his ears suddenly twitch and perk up. Bond's precognition is not absolute, and the future he sees can be changed if he takes a certain course of action. Notably, Anya acted upon Bond's precognition to prevent the death of Loid and the outbreak of civil war. Bond can even have a vision of him being unconscious, which is presented as an all-black scene, though it causes him to mistakenly interpret it as a premonition of his death.

Enhanced Speed and Agility: Bond shows himself to be very fast at running and can do so for long periods even with Anya on his back, allowing him to cover several grounds around the town. He has been shown to be able to outrun Yor, and he is athletic enough to perform a flying kick on an adult man and escape a burning building by jumping from a high floor.

Enhanced Smell: Being a dog, Bond has a highly attuned sense of smell, being able to detect Loid's scent while he was on the other side of the city. He was also trained to help detect explosives and flammable chemicals.

Basic Combat Training: Due to his past as a research subject for military purposes, Bond has likely been trained in basic combat abilities. In addition, Bond has received some training from Loid in incapacitating potential threats and has shown to be quite effective at bringing down full-grown adults.

Lack of Control Over His Power: Bond appears to have no control over his precognition, causing him to have visions spontaneously, and he can be shown different ones in a consecutive manner during a short period of time. This often causes him problems when he tries to prevent issues he foresees from happening, but it sometimes ends up being that he was going to cause the event in visions during his efforts.

entries.name: Becky Blackbell
entries.content:
“You and I should be best friends. After all, I'm the only one who knows how great you are!”
— Becky to Anya Forger

Becky Blackbell (ベッキー・ブラックベル, Bekkī Burakkuberu?) is one of the recurring characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. She is the daughter of the CEO of Blackbell Heavy Industries, a major military manufacturer in Ostania. She attends Eden Academy as a first-year student in Cecile Hall, Class 3, and is Anya Forger's best friend.

Becky is a young girl with fair skin and shoulder-length dark brown hair with uneven bangs that are swept to the side. Her eyes are light brown (hazel in the cover of Volume 9), narrow-shaped with double eyelids, and have prominent upper and lower eyelashes. Her eyebrows are thin and short, and there is usually a slight blush on her face.

Like all other female students, Becky is usually seen wearing Eden Academy's uniform. She also wears black knee-high socks and black shoes and carries around a brown schoolbag with a sheep keychain attached. During the interclass dodgeball match, Becky ties her hair with red ribbons when she is wearing the school gym uniform, along with black socks and gym shoes.

Becky's hair is typically tied into two side ponytails, and they are tied up with pink scrunchies. Her bangs are also usually held up with a hairclip that resembles a lit bomb. Depending on the occasion, Becky lets her hair down, and her hairclips tend to change, especially when she is going out. So far, Becky has worn hairclips of a fighter jet, a flower, a butterfly, Yor's earring, a heart arrow, an ammonite fossil, and a rose.

Becky is a very kind child, but as the daughter of an elite, she is shown to be somewhat prideful and tries to act more mature than she is, initially attempting to take Anya under her wing when she sees her as a brat. Becky does not attempt to get close to Damian Desmond despite his social position, even looking down on their classmates who try to befriend him. She also looked down on Anya when she was getting bullied by Damian's group during their orientation, but Anya's smug smile and defiance toward Damian later won over Becky's admiration and respect, after which the two girls became friends.

Despite their difference in social status, Becky genuinely cares about Anya and supports her, although some of Anya's words seem absurd or incomprehensible to her. She also cares what Anya thinks of her own actions and sometimes worries she is just dragging her along with her antics. When Anya gifts her a matching keychain as a sign of their friendship, Becky is touched by her friend's gesture and accepts it, although the keychain would be considered a cheap trinket compared to the more expensive gifts she is accustomed to receiving.

Becky is also quite patient, going along with Anya's desire to be called "Starlight Anya" after her success at getting a Stella Star, even though she quickly got annoyed by it. She is also a caring and protective girl as seen when she often confronts Damian whenever he bullies Anya, even promising to Anya that she will protect her no matter what.

Becky has proven to be fairly intelligent and academically gifted, ranking 42nd on her exam out of over 200 students, thus meeting Eden's overall standards. She also strives to be an idealized version of an adult by engaging in such hobbies as watching adult romance TV programs. However, this has made it difficult for her to associate with her peers, making her friendless for a while.

Becky is also seen to have a somewhat low outlook on monetary value, as seen when she shows little interest in mentioning how she gained presents such as a diamond-embedded doll and her own small house in her yard for doing well in school. At the same time, she is well aware of how rich she is. Her wealth often gives her what she wants, and periodically she willingly uses it to get what she desires. Becky is also capable of casually offending others by showing her surprise at their lower income, although sometimes she does not do this intentionally. She periodically demonstrates this trait with Anya. For example, Becky was not impressed with her friend's cash that her father gave her for their shopping trip, and when she visited Anya's home for a play date, Becky compared it with her larger home during the house tour, which prompted Anya to end it.

Becky is a romantic girl, being a big fan of romance movies and television shows like Berlint in Love, which she enjoys watching in her free time. She even thinks that Anya's efforts to get along with Damian are because Anya has a crush on him, so she often tries to help her win his heart. Becky is also aware of Damian's crush on Anya and teases him for it, and while she does not like him, she enjoys the perceived romance between him and her friend, believing that seeing their drama is better than her TV romances.

Becky can be mean, though she rarely shows this side of herself. Whenever arguing with Damian and his friends, she throws back just as nasty insults when they insult her and Anya. When George Glooman arrived at school the day after he claimed that he would have to leave Eden due to his family company's apparent bankruptcy, Becky coldly told him to return the gifts their classmates gave to him, which she later brought up as leverage to get a macaron from him.

Before meeting Anya, Becky used to act cocky and often engaged in fights with other kids after teasing them for their lower social position, which left her with no friends at all. The only bond she had besides her parents was with her butler Martha Marriott, who acts as a mother figure for Becky. Thanks to her friendship with Anya, Becky has changed her behavior toward others. Proof of this is when she invites Anya to go shopping together in order to help her friend get closer to Damian. While initially putting all of her efforts into helping Anya, Becky later focuses on buying dresses for herself to impress Anya's dad, Loid. After seeing Anya get exhausted from shopping, Becky worries she was dragging her friend along and nervously asks if she disliked their outing, but Anya answers that she had so much fun, which makes Becky feel genuinely happy. The girls then each get a sheep keychain as a memento of their trip and eventually forget the reason they went to buy clothes in the first place. Martha later points out that Anya is the first person Becky truly cares for.

Becky is still a child, so most of her known abilities are limited.

Strength: Becky strength is limited as she is a child, but she was taught some basic strength training and how to punch by Yor. When Damian annoys her and Anya, she threatens to hit him with a knockout punch, referring to the punch Yor taught them.

Intelligence: Despite Becky not being among the highest-grade students, she is very intelligent and studious since she has basic knowledge of many subjects. During her first term, Becky passed all of her midterm exams and ranked 42nd place overall. In the term finals, she passed all of her exams and moved up to 38th place overall.

Sense of Style: Despite her young age, Becky is already well-versed in fashion and modern trends. It seems that in her free time, she is a favorite customer in many stores where she often buys a lot of elegant outfits, and sometimes she even orders them at her home for a long fitting. In addition, Becky is able to choose fashionable outfits not only for herself but also to give fashion advice to others.

Crafting: Becky has been demonstrated to be quite competent at crafting. During an arts and crafts class, she created by herself a paper model of Loid and fashioned it with a paper combat suit replicating her father's company designs. She later created a paper model of a crocodile.

Maturity: Although at certain moments she becomes very self-centered and spoiled (which is understood by the environment in which she was raised), Becky comes to make decisions with maturity and responsibility as she is frequently advising and supporting of Anya, guiding and helping her in situations the girl does not understand. Even when Billy Squire and the Red Circus hijack their bus, despite being scared for Anya and herself, Becky devised a plan to let the people outside know about their current situation.

Because of her brave actions and quick thinking during the bus hijacking incident, Becky earns her first Stella Star alongside Anya, Damian, and Bill Watkins.

(To Anya): "People are so superficial. That or they just believe any dumb thing they hear […] You and I should be best friends. After all, I'm the only one who knows how great you are!"
(To Anya, about Damian): "Yeah, you never know what he might try to pull. But it doesn't matter! You have me on your side now! I'll protect you no matter what happens!"
(To herself, about Anya and Damian): "This is so great! TV romances are fun, but the real thing is incredible!"

entries.name: Henry Henderson
entries.content:
“Elegance is at the root of tradition. Elegance is what will bring about a better world.”
— Henry to the Eden teachers

Henry Henderson (ヘンリー・ヘンダーソン, Henrī Hendāson?) is one of the recurring characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. He is a History teacher and the housemaster of Dormitory 3, Cecile Hall at Eden Academy.

Henry has long, straight, white hair pulled into a tight ponytail ending just below his shoulders. His hairline is beginning to recede. He has a lengthy, straight, white beard cut in the Imperial style, with no hair on the chin but along the mustache and beard area without connecting to the head hair styled into two long points reaching his collarbone.

Taking into consideration his age, he has noticeable creases and wrinkles on his face, accompanied by small, thin eyes with thin eyebrows right above them. He is seen wearing a monocle on his left eye and usually has a stern expression, although significantly elegant things make him lose composure.

He is normally seen wearing a three-piece suit consisting of a dark jacket with long coattails and striped pants. He accessorizes with a pocket square, a tricolor striped tie, and a cane.

When Henry was younger, he had short hair, which he ended up growing to shoulder-length over the years. After his arrest, Henry cut his hair back short and began wearing his monocle after it was injured during his arrest.

Henry is a mature and noble person who places high importance on "elegance." To him, elegance seems to be the way a person conducts themselves and is not afraid to correct inelegant behavior in others. This can be seen in his interview with the Forger family, as he remained calm and composed even after Loid smashed the table between them after Murdoch Swan goaded the family, after which Henry himself punched the man after he threatened to silence Henry with his influence. In some cases, Henry will lose composure, usually when shocked or excited, like when he silently cursed to himself when Anya utterly failed to understand his words, or when he became elated by the Forgers' elegance and later frightened by how prepared they were during the first phase of the admissions.

Henry has an immense level of discipline, being able to exercise daily in the early morning and supervises the school's organization. When teaching and disciplining his students, Henry utilizes strict but sincere approach. He observes and assesses the "elegance" of the students, although he understands that the children occasionally need to frolic.

In his youth, Henry was an introverted boy, but as noble and disciplined as he currently is. His father once told him to "Be ever a gentleman," words that Henry would follow to a fault. While acting gentlemanly, Henry was a strict follower of the school rules and was always formal with fellow students and teachers, which would earn the ire of some of his peers, who believed he had a stuck-up attitude. When it came to getting into conflicts, Henry was firm on having civil conversations and refused to fight back to not stoop to the levels of animalistic behavior. However, he was willing to resort to violence to protect those he cared about or to defend his beliefs. Later, Henry transferred this quality to his old age, when he could not restrain himself and punched Murdoch Swan for his rude and inappropriate behavior towards the Forgers.

Henry grew up during the tense time between Ostania and Westalis, with the former preparing for war. In his final year at Eden, Henry was attacked by some students who held a grudge against him for his attitude and was saved by his junior Martha Marriott, which caused a skirmish. While protecting Martha, Henry punched one of his attackers and was ashamed that he resorted to such means. As such, he attempted to convince his teacher to punish him and his attackers for their violence. His teacher brushed the incident aside to avoid causing trouble with one of the boy's family members, who held great importance, which made Henry come to the belief that the Eden teachers have been corrupted.

After some thought, Henry concluded that by properly educating the youth into becoming proper characters, he could help end conflicts, whether it be petty fights or even global war, and decided that he would become a teacher. Henry became so obsessed with this ambition to radically change the world that he inadvertently pushed away not only his peers but also those close to him, particularly Martha. Two and a half years after his graduation from Eden, Henry returned to the school as a History teacher. During his first year as a teacher, Henry stubbornly believed that he could change the world if he stuck to his principles and chose to stay out of the ongoing war, which eventually drove a wedge between him and Martha, who left to join the war effort after graduating.

As the first war continued, Henry began realizing how much he cared for Martha as they kept in touch through letters. After believing that Martha had died on the frontlines, Henry grew embittered toward Ostania, especially the military, for her "death." An outburst denouncing the war during a military speech caused him to get arrested, after which his father arrived and told him to pull himself together at the risk of his teaching career. Envisioning a peaceful future with the students that Martha once told him about in her letters, Henry decided to work toward making such a future happen, realizing it mattered more than his pride.

Organization: As Cecile Hall's housemaster, Henry supervises both the students and the caretakers of the house. He is in charge of ensuring the students are completing chores and going to classes, as well as directing the other staff, such as the gardeners and cleaners.

Discipline: One of Henry's tasks is to maintain authority over the students and may take disciplinary action in the case of misconduct.

Teaching: Henry is a highly-respected educator, primarily teaching History. He does not compromise his standards when it comes to teaching, speaking with students, or grading them. Henry also gives supplementary lessons for students who are struggling in class. On some occasions, he even fills in for absent teachers, such as the gym teacher and art teacher.

Athleticism: Henry is remarkably fit for his age, as evidenced by his daily regimen of taking a jog early in the morning and the impact force he generated when he punched Murdoch Swan following the Forgers' interview at Eden. It is also noted that he is good at horse riding.

(To himself): "Those who grovel at the feet of the powerful have no right to call themselves educators!"
(To Thomas Austin): "From the grand efforts with which our forefathers crafted society to the foolish ideas that sent them racing to war... to not study the human element at history's root is to not understand history at all."
(To himself, watching Damian Desmond and his friends): "There's nothing more elegant than the precious elegance of youthful friendship!"
(To Anya Forger): "You must not regard Stella Stars and Imperial Scholarship so lightly, Miss Forger. They are the symbols of Eden Academy's reputation over five centuries. Behold, Miss Forger. These are the faces of students whose diligent studies led them to greatness. Politicians, artists, athletes, scholars, engineers, and more. Imperial Scholars, every last one of them. Through ceaseless, painstaking effort and unflagging self-control, by never letting failure quell their drive to succeed, honing themselves through rivalries and partnerships, they all managed to achieve the title of "Imperial Scholar." Nothing of import is ever accomplished in a day, Miss Forger."
(To himself): "Discord was being sown throughout the world. As arsenals swell... grudges deepen... and poverty grows. We've allowed education to fall by the wayside."
(To himself): "I was the most hard-headed of idealists back then. I still believed that the world would change as long as I heeded my principles. so I dug in to defend something that was worth nothing. Education is, at its heart, the act of influencing and inspiring others. But, like a clown in a farce ...I, the man who waxed poetic about the value of education, had failed to refute a single one of Martha's arguments. It wasn't education that was powerless. I was powerless."

entries.name: Emile Elman
entries.content:
“I guess I just want to be able to eat a lot of candy.”
— Emile to Mr. Green

Emile Elman (エミール・エルマン, Emīru Eruman?) is one of the supporting characters of the SPY X FAMILY series. He is the heir of the Elman family who attends Eden Academy as a first-year student in Cecile Hall, Class 3, and is one of Damian Desmond's followers and friends.

Emile is a young boy with a square face and slanted eyes with small black irises (sometimes green in the anime). He has a round physique, an upturned nose, buckteeth, and blond hair that is styled into a bowl cut.

Like all other male students, Emile wears Eden Academy's uniform—a black button-up shirt with black shorts. He also wears white crew socks with black shoes.

As one of Damian's followers alongside Ewen, Emile frequently praises Damian's abilities and makes fun of Anya and Becky, but he is good at doing the right thing to save Damian. Emile is willing to sacrifice himself for Damian during the dodgeball tournament, throwing himself in the path of Bill Watkins's ball. He also jumps into the river without hesitance when he assumes Damian is drowning.

Emile does not have any future aspirations when he grows up but has stated that it is his dream to eat a lot of candy, and he has also shown to be interested in getting Stella Stars and becoming Imperial Scholars with Damian and Ewen.

Damian is Emile's friend and classmate in Cecile Hall. He has known him and Ewen since nursery school. Emile displays great loyalty to Damian, even deciding not to join the other boys to watch a movie and have roast beef during the holiday to instead help Damian do chores around the dorm, willingly getting himself punished by Henry Henderson in order to do so. He also displays great admiration for Damian, always praising his abilities. This faith in Damian is so great that Emile has declared that if Damian ever gets a Tonitrus Bolt, the trio will go through Eden Academy in their underpants, much to Damian's reluctance to uphold that.

Emile is a selfless boy and is even willing to sacrifice himself for Damian's sake, as shown when he jumps in the way of a dodgeball thrown by Bill to protect Damian from getting hit and allow him the chance of being the MVP of their dodgeball match. Later, when the boys go on a field research trip with Mr. Green, Emile quickly jumps in after Damian when he sees him fall overboard from their canoe, and when the boys believe they are drowning, Emile prioritizes Damian's safety over his own. During the Red Circus bus hijacking, in which Damian had a bomb attached to him (which most were unaware that it was actually fake), Emile did not even consider running away to protect his friend's life.

Despite his fervent loyalty to Damian, Emile also shows a mischievous streak toward him, as he and Ewen gleefully chase him around with earthworms upon learning of Damian's fear of them. Emile is also not afraid to be humorous around Damian, even if it is at Damian's expense, such as when he and Ewen tease him for looking like Anya's "twin" after she accidentally spills a yakisoba burger on his head.

At the start of their second school term, Emile and Ewen come to believe that Damian has another, more important friend. As such, Emile decides to work hard to prove to Damian that he and Ewen are friends he can rely on by helping solve his problem. After Mr. Green gives the boys advice on dealing with their jealousy at not being Damian's most important friends, they visualize their jealousy as a "Mr. Buzz" character, whom Emile embraces. After the misunderstanding is resolved by Damian, Emile and Ewen are relieved to be his true friends.

Ewen is Emile's friend and classmate in Cecile Hall and has known him and Damian since nursery school. Both of them work with Damian to become Imperial Scholars together and are always ready to support him, with both agreeing that their "hearts beat as one" with Damian.

Anya is Emile's classmate in Cecile Hall but currently does not get along with her because of Damian. When they first meet at the school orientation, Emile pushes Anya away from Damian so he does not catch her "peasant germs." After Anya punches Damian, Emile becomes defensive of Damian and tries to keep her away from hurting him again. Whenever they interact, Emile makes fun of her and calls her names, usually mocking her appearance and commoner status. However, in some instances when Anya would cry or smile, Emile would react with a blush alongside Damian.

Becky is also Emile's classmate in Cecile Hall and is currently on bad terms with her for being Anya's best friend and her snarky attitude toward him and his friends. Whenever the two interact, they are usually seen arguing.

entries.name: Ewen Egeburg
entries.content:
“Don't worry. Once Damian is grown up, I know he'll make Ostania a better place to live!”
— Ewen to Mr. Green

Ewen Egeburg (ユーイン・エッジバーグ, Yūin Ejjibāgu?) is one of the supporting characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. He is the heir of the Egeburg family who attends Eden Academy as a first-year student in Cecile Hall, Class 3, and is one of Damian Desmond's followers and friends.

Ewen is a young boy with light skin and an elongated head. He has relatively tiny, square-shaped eyes with small black pupils (sometimes blue in the anime). Ewen's hair is his unique feature, larger than his own head and blond and combed back. When his hair is down, it reaches about chin-length.

Like all other male students, Ewen wears Eden Academy's uniform—a black button-up shirt with black shorts. He also wears long white crew socks with black shoes. During their mornings on their way to Eden Academy, Ewen typically holds another bag in his arms along with his own bag on his back, the former likely to be Damian's bag.

Ewen first appears to be another arrogant child at Eden Academy and Damian's lackey, but he has shown that he is a loyal friend who has Damian's best interests at heart. Alongside Emile, Ewen is devoted to Damian and always follows him wherever he goes, even carrying his bag on their way to class. Ewen genuinely cares for Damian as a friend, getting concerned for him when he is hurt or pushing himself too hard.

Ewen has an affinity for space exploration, so much to the point that it is his dream to become a cosmonaut in the future. He claims to have an appreciation for the romance of space exploration and is genuinely upset that his friends do not share the same passion, thus finding joy upon finding others who also like space adventures, even someone like Anya.

Ewen shows great respect for Damian, who is the leader of their clique. He looks up to Damian and places lots of faith in him, believing that Damian will make their country a better place when he becomes a politician. Regarding this, they are shown to be good friends and spend a lot of time together. Ewen calls him Lord Damian and usually does everything he asks for, even holding his backpack when walking to class. Despite this, he and Emile also show a mischievous streak toward Damian, chasing him around with an earthworm upon learning of Damian's fear, and they are not afraid to make jokes at his expense. Ewen is oblivious to Damian's crush on Anya and believes the two are enemies.

At the start of their second school term, Ewen and Emile come to believe that Damian has another, more important friend. Ewen, who values his friendship with Damian, feels hurt about the revelation and begins wondering why he and Emile continue to support him. After Mr. Green gives the boys advice on dealing with their jealousy at not being Damian's most important friends, they visualize their jealousy as a "Mr. Buzz" character, whom Ewen quietly acknowledges. After the misunderstanding is resolved by Damian, Ewen and Emile are relieved to be his true friends.

Emile is Ewen's friend. Both of them work with Damian and are his closest confidants, even saying that their hearts beat as one with his.

Since their orientation, Ewen has been on bad terms with Anya after she punched Damian, wanting to protect his friend from what he believes is a violent person. Ewen also looks down on Anya because of her lower class status, calling her a peasant and taking any opportunity he can get to belittle her. After their term finals, Ewen is upset that Anya got a Stella Star for academics before he did.

The two briefly shared a bonding moment when Ewen discovered that Anya also enjoys space adventure, prompting him to tell her all he knows about it and pretending to be an astronaut crew together.

As Becky is Anya's best friend, Ewen is also on bad terms with her, getting into heated arguments when their respective groups have their usual squabbles.

entries.name: Bill Watkins
entries.content:
“The son of Chairman Desmond is concerned for me. I'm honored. But you don't need to worry, Damian. I won't be getting hit.”
— Bill to Damian Desmond

Bill Watkins (ビル・ワトキンス, Biru Watokinsu?) is one of the supporting characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. He is the son of a major in Ostania's national army who attends Eden Academy as a first-year student in Wald Hall, Class 4.

Due to being an early bloomer, Bill is a young boy who is considerably taller and incredibly muscular for his age when compared to his peers. He has short brown hair, thick eyebrows, and blue eyes, which are hidden by reflective glasses.

Like all other male students, Bill wears Eden Academy's uniform—a black button-up shirt with black shorts. He also wears white crew socks with black shoes.

Befitting his more mature appearance and family profession, Bill is an extremely disciplined boy who approaches virtually all matters with utmost seriousness. Above all, Bill's main drive is to make his father proud, as he has an immense amount of respect and love for him. To this end, Bill regularly trains his body and mind to maximize his potential, even if it is for something as simple as a game of dodgeball. This results in him having a great deal of confidence in his skills, which will immediately falter should his normally well-calculated plans fail.

While he often tries to act more mature, Bill sometimes lets his demeanor slip and acts more his age, like when he began to cry after failing to eliminate Anya with his dodgeball throws or when spending time with his father. Outside of dodgeball competitions, Bill also appears to be a relaxed and kind boy. He seems to be well-liked by his classmates in Wald Hall and is also welcome to the idea of befriending others outside of his circle, such as when he attempted to befriend Damian at the start of their field trip to the museum and when he agreed with Anya's sentiments to stick with their friend group longer during the city's Winter Festival.

Bill is shown to be somewhat chivalrous, using far less force when competing against girls to avoid injuring them, though in extreme situations he will forsake this mindset for absolute victory. When Donna Schlag returned to Eden Academy and struck Wald Hall with Tonitruses, Bill went out of his way to warn his schoolmates in Cecile Hall about Lady Tonitrus and urged them to flee. Bill also displays immense courage, as during the bus hijacking by the Red Circus, he bravely stood up to announce to his schoolmates that help would come. Despite quickly cowering after being threatened by the group's leader, Billy Squire, Bill's words manage to get through to his peers and temporarily calm them down.

Enhanced Strength: Despite only being a child, Bill is incredibly strong after enduring lots of training from his father. He is able to throw a ball with enough force to demolish standard military training targets and even bend a metal lamp post.

Analytical Mind: Bill can make very complicated calculations very quickly after lots of studying. He uses this to his advantage during the inter-class dodgeball match where he is able to eliminate several opponents with a single throw.

Homing Slider Shot
(ホーミングスライダーショット,
Hōmingu Suraidā Shotto?) Bill's secret move during the interclass dodgeball game. It is a throw that changes course in midair, best suited for opponents who move around while dodging. Bill attempts to use this move on Anya, who hears him explaining the technique in his thoughts and dodges it by staying still.

Wesley is Bill's father, whom he has an immense amount of respect and love for, and he tries to live up to his expectations as the future of Ostania's army. When they are together, Bill drops his more serious demeanor and affectionately refers to his father as "daddy." However, Wesley's orders appear to sometimes intimidate Bill, as when he decides to join the game of ring toss against the girls, Wesley commands that Bill be withdrawn from Eden if he fails to win the game, which Bill reluctantly agrees to.

Damian is one of Bill's rivals aiming to earn a Stella Star at the interclass dodgeball match. At the start of the game, they briefly banter after Damian tries to eliminate him. Later, they meet again when he tries to warn Anya and the rest of her classmates that Donna Schlag is giving Tonitrus Bolts to everyone. When Wald Hall and Cecile Hall share a bus during a trip to the museum, Bill finds himself seated behind Damian. Bill proposes becoming friends, but Damian states their classes are rivals. In response, Bill challenges him to see which class can name the most dinosaurs in the museum. After the bus gets hijacked by the Red Circus, Bill and Damian do selfless acts to calm their classmates, earning each other's respect.

They met on the day of the interclass dodgeball match. After whittling down most of Cecile Hall's team, Bill tries to hit Anya many times, but fails at every single attempt, as she is able to read his mind to predict where he would throw the ball. Anya scares Bill when she attempts to throw the ball at him with all her strength, but to no avail, as she only lets the ball bounce right to Bill's feet, allowing him to grab it and throw it back to her with little effort. Later, they meet again when he tries to warn Anya and the rest of her classmates that Donna Schlag is giving Tonitrus Bolts to everyone. During the bus hijacking, Bill and the rest of his peers are unnerved by Anya's unusual calmness despite getting a bomb attached to her neck. By the end of the hijacking, he appears to respect her bravery in the face of danger.

Because of his brave actions to calm and support his classmates during the bus hijacking incident, Bill earns his first Stella Star alongside Anya, Becky, and Damian.
Bill earns his second Stella for the second highest score in Math term finals.

entries.name: George Glooman
entries.content:
“Be careful not to lie too much. Or you'll end up becoming an outcast like me.”
— George to Anya Forger

George Glooman (ジョージ・グルーマン, Jōji Gurūman?) is one of the supporting characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. He attends Eden Academy as a first-year student in Cecile Hall, Class 3.

George is a young boy with a triangle-shaped head, short black hair, and black eyes.

Like all other male students, he wears Eden Academy's uniform—a black button-up shirt with black shorts. George also wears long white crew socks with black shoes.

George is described as always being gloomy, causing him to be an outcast in his class. He appears to be jealous of Damian and his family for their reputation and accomplishments and developed a hatred for them after initially believing his father's company, Glooman Pharmaceuticals, was driven out of the market because of the Desmonds, going as far as hiring a spy with the help of his old butler to rig Damian and his brother's midterm answers.

Despite his negative traits, George is an ordinary, vulnerable child who is easily offended and upset when he feels injustice toward himself. He also has a sensitive side, which manifested itself when he said goodbye to his classmates who decided to support him when leaving school.

George often silently observes others and seems to have some insight, at least when he sees that someone is lying. Although Anya's lies about her cruise trip quickly became apparent, George was one of the first to realize that she was tricking to make an impression, but he did not interfere, watching the development of events from afar. Later, when Anya is ridiculed by her classmates and leaves school together with Becky, George shows an unexpected interest in her fate and gives the girl valuable advice based on his bitter experience. George told Anya that she shouldn't lie a lot if she didn't want to become an outcast like him, thus showing that he is uncomfortable with the situation in which he found himself because of his own lie.

Manipulator: George appears to be particularly good at making people believe him, as shown when he almost achieves his goal of getting Damian in trouble with the teacher had Anya not intervened. Later, he manages to gain the sympathy of his classmates by telling them his story, making them grant his final requests before his presumed departure from Eden Academy, and, by the end of the day, he goes home with keepsakes from each of his classmates and a bouquet. However, most likely he did it so well because he sincerely believed that he would have to leave school and be sold into slavery in Westalis, until his father informed him of the true state of their affairs.

He tried this tactic again when Becky and Damian demanded for his set of Pierre Pommier Macarons by claiming he used the little money he had on them, but it failed due to the fact he still owes them for the stuff they had given him.

At first, George hated Damian for always being the perfect boy with good grades, to the point of going to great lengths to try to make Damian get a Tonitrus, and even tried to have him expelled. After George explained his jealousy towards him and his family status and claimed he would be leaving Eden, Damian and other Cecile Hall students helped him fulfill his wishes, with Damian even lending George his Stella Star. Afterward, Damian and the other students gave George their belongings so he could remember them. The next day George returns to school, having to endure an embarrassing moment as Damian and the other kids ask him to return all the things they gave him.

After a long time, George never returned Damian's things. Later, when they were on the bus, George tacitly decided to demand sweets from Damian, believing that Damian owed him for the macaron he had once taken. However, Damian viciously disagrees with this statement, loudly reminding George that he did not receive anything, and his anger brings George to frightened tears.

entries.name: Donovan Desmond
entries.content:
“Our children may share our blood, but they aren't us. They're essentially strangers. It is impossible to understand strangers. In the end… people will never truly be sympathetic with each other.”
— Donovan to his son and Loid Forger

Donovan Desmond (ドノバン・デズモンド, Donoban Dezumondo?) is the chairman of the National Unity Party of Ostania and Twilight's target for his current mission. He is the main antagonist of the SPY x FAMILY series.

Donovan is a tall and slim middle-aged man with sunken black eyes that are seemingly always open in a perfectly circular shape, closely shaved black hair with noticeable graying streaks on his left side, a black mustache, and a lack of eyebrows. He has pierced ears and a line of scars on the sides of his head. On his left hand, Donovan also wears a ring on his ring finger.

Donovan's attire consists of a tan suit that covers a white polo shirt with a black tie that is held together using a brooch with a golden-yellow star-shaped symbol and a pair of brown shoes.

When Donovan was a middle school student at Eden Academy, he had a disconnected bowl cut and wore the school's standard uniform for boys. Compared to his current appearance, the younger Donovan appeared more bright-eyed. In past photographs and memories, it is shown that he had more hair than he does now, especially on the sides of his head, and had a few loose curls hanging from his hairline.

Donovan is a recluse and extremely suspicious of others, and he has been described as inscrutable by Loid upon their first meeting. Since losing power as the Prime Minister of Ostania, Donovan has been very cautious and rarely makes public appearances. However, he regularly attends social gatherings at Eden Academy for his elder son, Demetrius. On these outings, Donovan travels with a large security team, with four core men surrounding him at all times. Donovan appears to keep a distance from others, especially strangers, as when Loid insists on going to his manor to make a proper apology, Donovan twice rejects him cordially, hinting to the man to back off.

As the patriarch of the Desmonds, Donovan seems to place great importance on their family name, something he urges his younger son, Damian, not to besmirch. Mysteriously, despite his emphasis, he was not offended but rather indifferent to the fact that Anya hit Damian, and even when Loid apologized for the event, he easily accepted it as a childish spat and forgave it. In his younger years, he bluntly told his recently disgraced teacher Henry Henderson that he thought him to be a fool and said that "one shouldn't expect anything of those who, in their foolishness, have disappointed you once already."

He also appears to place importance on achievements, as he is negligent toward the less successful Damian. This motivates the boy to seek out as many successes as he can to get his father's attention. He shows further indifference when Damian tries to question him for dismissing Anya's punching of him by simply letting out a long and audible sigh until Damian lets it go. Later in their conversation, when Damian tells Donovan about his recent achievements at school, the man barely reacts and tells his son "Good for you."

During his school years, Donovan talked about his desire for peace like anyone else but had a firm belief that humans are liars who will never be free of war. Years later, during his conversation with Loid, Donovan shares his belief that people can never truly sympathize with each other, even to the point of thinking of his own children as strangers. Loid alludes that this may be why he seeks to cause war, in order to control others through military force.

According to the story of Donovan's wife, Melinda, he was not originally a paranoid recluse during their time together. Sometime between the births of their sons, Donovan had a shift in personality and became a completely different person who started pushing everyone around him away and barely speaking to anyone. This change has alienated Donovan from his family, as they fail to understand the reasons for his mysterious actions and choices to avoid or spend time with them.

While Donovan is a closed-off individual, he appears to make exceptions and other mysterious actions. Despite his busy schedule, Donovan agrees to meet with Damian after the Imperial Scholars mixer, which Loid suggests was his attempt to understand his estranged son better, though Donovan later tells Damian that it was just on a whim. He also does not appear to worry when talking to Loid, the father of his son's attacker and who is described by the boy as a "peasant," as he allows him a chance to speak with him, showing that he does not seem to care too much about his interlocutor's status. However, as Loid left the conversation, Donovan shared quiet glares with him before shifting his focus to Damian.

(On the topic: "Can we ever free ourselves of war?"): "We will never be free of war. History is clear proof of that. But what if we purged all weapons from the world? Even then, no. Because in the end... human beings are simply liars. We'd ask, 'What if other nations have kept some weapons in secret?' And so long as that doubt persisted, history would be doomed to repeat itself. We can never know the true intentions of others. Because we ourselves are hiding our true intentions. Of course, I desire peace as much as anyone. And I know that solving differences with dialogue instead of weapons is ideal. But warring like this is the best we humans are capable of. Even if there were resources left over... even if there were governmental reform or a technological innovation, I can't imagine an end to war."

entries.name: Melinda Desmond
entries.content:
“I know I asked you to come see us again, as if it were no big deal... but if there are any, say, political considerations that make it uncomfortable for you, I understand. That said… If it's still possible… I do hope you and I can be friends, Yor.”
— Melinda to Yor Forger

Melinda Desmond (メリンダ・デズモンド, Merinda Dezumondo?) is the wife of Donovan Desmond and mother of Demetrius and Damian Desmond. She is also the chairwoman of the Lady Patriots Society.

Melinda is a beautiful and fairly tall woman. She has dark brown hair, hazel eyes, and fair skin with a beauty mark on the lower right side of her mouth. Similar to Damian, her eyes are narrowed and droop slightly, with visibly long lower eyelashes and short, thin eyebrows above. She wears dangling triangular-shaped earrings with an inscribed circle and a small black dot in the middle. On her left hand, she wears a ring on her ring finger, and on her right is a ring on her middle finger with the triangle and circle symbol engraved on it.

Melinda has been shown to typically wear a disguise when going out in public, wearing a bandana around her head and sunglasses to cover her face. She appears to be athletic and organizes the Lady Patriots Society, which she leads to participate in sports games like volleyball.

While dressed as fortune teller Lunaluna☽Selena, Melinda wears an indigo-colored fortune teller's outfit with a face veil and a masquerade mask to conceal her identity.

Melinda is an energetic and cheerful lady who hides a dark, conflicting nature. While with others inside her circle, Melinda is kind and sociable. When she first meets Yor and witnesses her amazing physical skills, she immediately takes a liking to Yor and wants to befriend her. While spending time together, Melinda treats Yor kindly, patiently teaching her to work with a team and encouraging her to enjoy herself. As she does not have a lot of friends she can be herself around, Melinda does not appear worry too much about status and wants those around her to be themselves. As such, when she first talks with Yor, Melinda deliberately hides her identity from her, as she genuinely wanted to be friends with Yor without any preconceptions. Melinda also seems to be a little naive, as she believed that she would get kicked when Yor mentions that Loid practices "concussive therapy," to the point of refusing to be treated by Loid if he ever performs it on her, and even trying to defend herself from him when they first meet.

As a member of the Desmond family and the former First Lady of Ostania, Melinda acts with grace and maturity, as she is aware of who she represents and seeks to uphold the duties those roles have. She also shows an empathetic side, as seen when Yor's co-worker, Millie Myers, who lost her father to the second East-West war, accuses Donovan of starting the war and associates Melinda with him. In response, Melinda apologizes to Millie and empathizes with her feelings, sharing that she also has her own family and would resent someone if she lost any of them. Afterward, she kindly thanks Millie for helping at the event, and her respect is returned as Millie apologizes for her words. Additionally, as the chairwoman of the Lady Patriots Society, Melinda wants a good reputation for the group, discouraging her members from making unsightly displays of themselves and policing others' behaviors.

Similar to Donovan, Melinda also has a small and exclusive circle around her. Following the National Unity Party's loss of power, Melinda stopped involving herself in politics, mainly communicating with her household staff and the few close friends whom she knew before she became the First Lady. She also stopped making public appearances, but when she goes outside for outings or helps at city events with the Lady Patriots Society, Melinda always wears a disguise. One of Melinda's closely kept secrets is her hobby of practicing divination as a fortune teller. Melinda believes in destiny and mysticism, and, likely due to her suspicions about her husband, keeps an open mind about the existence of supernatural things like ghosts, UFOs, telepathy, and so on. She genuinely enjoys her hobby and admits that it is one of the few things that brings her comfort. However, she keeps this secret as it could negatively affect Donovan and others around them, as well as out of embarrassment, believing a woman of her age and status should not like those sorts of things.

In private, however, Melinda is a much different person, filled with anxiety and paranoia. Following Donovan's sudden change into becoming a quiet recluse after losing power, Melinda became wary of her husband's shift in personality, which eventually grew into an intense fear of him as she became convinced that he could read minds. This later developed into Melinda believing that Donovan was taken away by an alien who assumed his identity. Unsure of what her husband has become, Melinda has tried to protect herself from him, which takes all she has and leaves no room to protect their two sons as well.

As such, whenever Donovan randomly decides to engage with the boys or ignore them completely, Melinda willingly follows along, even though she has never been ordered to do so. For example, when Yor tried apologizing for Anya punching Damian during their school orientation, Melinda brushed it off with a laugh, citing that Donovan did the same, then shut down Yor with an unexpectedly cold expression when she insisted further. As a result of this distancing, the Desmonds have become estranged from each other. This greatly pains Melinda, who wishes to be more of a mother to her sons, especially her youngest, Damian. Although Melinda genuinely loves Damian and hopes the best for him, for reasons currently unknown, her fear of Donovan seems to have distorted her view of him, as she views him as a curse that she often wishes would go away. Melinda's suffering from this has reached to a point that she, at Yor's recommendation, visits Loid for a consultation to discuss her problems with him.

Athleticism: Melinda appears to be quite an active woman, as she engages in volleyball games with the Lady Patriots Society.

Fortune-Telling: Melinda secretly practices divination as a fortune teller while under the alias Lunaluna☽Selena. Although it is her hobby, Melinda is not very good at it. She is well aware of this weakness, admitting to others that she is a total amateur and even sharing it in her own advertisements. At best, Melinda appears to have basic knowledge of the practice, knowing the tarot cards used in fortune-telling and their readings, including the Major Arcana. However, she does not understand the Minor Arcana cards, nor is she completely confident in her interpretations.

Medical Disorders: Due to her fear of Donovan and the strain she feels from her family situation, Melinda has been stressed to the point that she suffers from headaches, insomnia, and a diminished appetite.

(To Damian Desmond, about Donovan Desmond): "Of course I won't tell him. But in exchange, you absolutely cannot let that man know that I came here. Promise?"
(To Millie Myers): "I know that this will not help atone for all that you've suffered. But I have parents too. I have children of my own. And a husband, of course. Were I to lose any of them, I'm sure I would resent someone for it too."

entries.name: Demetrius Desmond
entries.content:
“I don't understand people. Enough of this. Who cares? Pondering it is such a waste of time.”
— Demetrius to himself

Demetrius Desmond (デミトリアス・デズモンド, Demitoriasu Dezumondo?) is the first son of the Desmond Family and the older brother of Damian Desmond. He attends Eden Academy as an eighth-year student in Cline Hall, Class 2, and is also an Imperial Scholar.

Demetrius is an exceptional student, barely getting a single question wrong on the midterm exams and earning six Stella Stars in the recent term finals.

Demetrius is a tall and slim teenage boy with medium-length and slightly curly dark brown hair which is combed back. He also has fair skin and big, light eyes that are slightly shaped downwards. He generally resembles a younger version of his father, Donovan, but in his gloomy mood, he slightly resembles his mother, Melinda.

At home, Demetrius has a more relaxed appearance, letting his hair down with a few loose curls hanging from his hairline, similar to his father's past appearance.

Like other Imperial Scholars, he is usually seen wearing Eden Academy's uniform and a black cape with a dark red lining and a gold cord holding it together at the chest.

Demetrius is as secretive and cold as his parents and has an extremely narrow circle of communication (in his case, those being other Imperial Scholars). Mysteriously, when Anya initially tries reading his mind, it is completely silent. When she does get to hear his thoughts, he thinks about how he does not understand people and that thinking about it is a waste of time, showing himself to be highly unsociable, even toward his family. Nevertheless, it is clear that he is a versatile genius who earns his father's favoritism and participates in various fields to achieve achievements and glorify his family. It also seems that he is a fairly honest and straightforward person and appears to be quite stoic and silent, saying few words only when being spoken to and never starting a conversation by himself.

Athleticism: Demetrius appears to have advanced skills in some sports. Ewen and Emile have admired his achievements in a photo album and praised him as a genuine MVP.

Genius-level Intellect: Loid called Demetrius an exceptional student. Demetrius is extraordinarily smart and erudite in academics, as he almost never makes mistakes in his works, and in the term finals, he earned Stellas in six subjects that consisted of mathematics, biology, physics, history, and two different languages.

Little is known about their relationship, but it appears that the two used to be close. When Demetrius was little, it was said that Donovan barely left his son's side and always watched him study, perhaps due to Demetrius being an outstanding student and a worthy representative of the family. In the past, it is implied that he (and Melinda) came to Demetrius's orientation when he first entered Eden and were in a group photo that was not done for Damian, which perhaps indicates some of Donovan's favoritism for his elder son. When Anya reads his mind, she hears that Demetrius does not understand his father after talking with Damian, who asks if he said anything about his achievement on the term finals.

It is unknown how their relationship currently stands, but it is implied they have become strained through years, as Demetrius tells Damian that they are not in regular contact with each other, contrary to the younger Desmond's initial belief.

When the Desmond family reunites to have dinner together for the first time in a long while, Demetrius does not talk with Donovan at all during their mealtime, keeping to himself while eating his dinner. The only time Demetrius talks to Donovan is after he quietly finishes his meal, tidies himself, and sits upright. Donovan responds to his actions by dismissing Demetrius from the table, after which the boy thanks his father before leaving the dining room.

According to Melinda, Demetrius has said that Donovan can read minds. It is likely a large factor behind his seemingly empty mind when Anya tries to read it and also his inability to understand his father.

According to Loid, Melinda is somewhat estranged from her husband and sons, which makes it clear that Demetrius has a distant relationship with his mother.

Their estrangement is displayed when the Desmonds have dinner as a family for the first time in a long while. During the dinner, Demetrius barely interacts with his mother and vice-versa, as both keep to themselves the entire time. When Demetrius is the first to leave the table after finishing his meal, Melinda uses his departure to exit the room as soon as she can, quickly following suit despite barely touching her own food.

Damian is Demetrius's little brother. Not much is known about their past, but they appear to have been distant ever since Damian was young. It seems that Demetrius has an extremely icy attitude toward his brother, so much so that he hardly even wants to talk to him on the phone, throwing only short neutral phrases. Nevertheless, he seems to have no problem fulfilling his request to pass the message to their father, but he also bluntly states that the kid should not have much hope because he may not come.

After the end-of-term awards ceremony, Damian approaches Demetrius once again and does not give up trying to be friendly with him by congratulating him on his awards, but Demetrius responds by coldly asking if that was all he came to him to say. However, when he watches Damian stumbling over his words, Demetrius pauses before mentioning Damian's own award and thinks about how he cannot understand his little brother. Demetrius's topic causes Damian to bring up Donovan again, asking for any reactions from him. Following this, Demetrius does not want to continue further conversations, stunning Damian as he reveals that he and their father do not maintain regular contact.

During the brothers' school break, Damian decides to return to their family estate, where Demetrius is also present, though he remains in his room for most of the day. Demetrius is visited by Damian, who knocks on his bedroom door in the hopes of receiving help for some homework. Without even opening the door to talk with his brother, Demetrius rejects him and directs him to their staff tutor. Later that day, when the family reunites for a rare family dinner, Demetrius does not interact with Damian at all, despite sitting across from him at the table, and quietly keeps to himself the entire time.

Before the events of the series, Demetrius earned eight Stellas for unknown achievements and became an Imperial Scholar. It seems that he received some of his Stellas for his athletic and academic achievements.
Demetrius earns 6 Stellas for his high score in subjects ranging from Math, History, Biology, Physics, Primary Foreign Language, and Secondary Foreign Language.

(To Damian, referring to Donovan): "I'll tell him. But don't get your hopes up. He's a busy man."

entries.name: Damian Desmond
entries.content:
“I'm Damian, scion of the Desmond family! I'll be a politician one day and protect this country! Father fought against all kinds of enemies during the war… and I… can fight too!”
— Damian to himself

Damian Desmond (ダミアン・デズモンド, Damian Dezumondo?) is one of the recurring characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. He is the second son of Donovan and Melinda Desmond and is also the younger brother of Demetrius Desmond. He attends Eden Academy as a first-year student in Cecile Hall, Class 3, and is Anya Forger's classmate and rival.

Damian is a young boy with short dark brown (sometimes blackish-brown) hair, hazel eyes, and light skin. Similar to his mother, Damian's eyes are narrowed and slightly drooping, with visibly long lower eyelashes and short, thin eyebrows above them. In the anime, his hair periodically has a greenish tinge. Damian often wears a condescending expression. In Anya's perspective, he gains a more stupider appearance with round, wide eyes.

Like other students, Damian is usually seen wearing Eden Academy's uniform. He also wears socks with vertical lines and black shoes.

One of Damian's casual clothing consists of him wearing a white vest with a golden "D" emblem imprinted on the top left side over a light blue or dark purple long-sleeved buttoned shirt of choice, blackish pants, and brown shoes. He still retains his striped socks in this outfit.

Due to his upbringing as the child of an important and powerful man, Damian gained a highly respected status among his peers by default, making him grow incredibly arrogant, assuming Anya gained a crush on him when he caught her staring at him. He is shown to prefer being called "Lord Damian" when spoken to. He gets angry when he is looked down upon by Anya's smug smile, quickly resorting to insulting her with his limited vocabulary and harassing Anya.

After taking a punch from Anya, he becomes very embarrassed around her. After Anya's tear-filled apology, Damian develops a crush on her that he does not want to acknowledge, denying it at every opportunity he gets.

Later, it is hinted that a possible reason for Damian's behavior can be attributed to his brother's success as an Imperial Scholar and his father's influence which has set high expectations for him to strive and become part of the Imperial Scholars. Damian believes that getting a high status and achieving success will encourage his honored father to finally pay attention to him. These lofty ambitions very often encourage him to neglect others and even his own rest. Periodically, Damian allows himself to relax and be an ordinary child who likes to have fun and spend time with his friends. Although even in a playful manner, the boy may show signs of irritation or even anger if someone or something prevents him from achieving any merit.

The desire to become the pride of his father is the main motivator for Damian to make progress in various types of activities. This causes him to look down on others beneath his social class for if they are not a benefit to him, they only slow him down from becoming an Imperial Scholar and in turn, slow down his progress. Damian also has a fairly developed competitive spirit when he is ready to overcome not only himself but also intentionally step over others on the way to achieving his goals.

Despite his high ambitions, Damian is capable of self-sacrifice to the detriment of his interests. A rare exception is when he protects Anya from a ball in a dodgeball game, willingly getting himself eliminated. Though it did not help their class win the game, Anya recognized Damian's good nature. Another rare moment was in their classroom when a girl from their class was spreading a rude rumor about how Anya got her first Stella Star, Damian stood up for her, recognizing Anya's merit, although still mentally outraged that she was ahead of him in receiving the award. Damian would even offer his school supply case to George Glooman when he was told that he would be moving, though he would later demand George to return all the stuff he gave him after figuring out that this was not the case. During the bus hijacking by the Red Circus, he showed bravery and selflessness when he tried to save Anya, demanding that the terrorists give the bomb on her to him instead.

Behind his cocky, self-absorbed, snobby behavior is a sweet, insecure boy desperate for his parents' love and approval. After the bus hijacking incident, Damian is surprised and tearfully relieved that his mother came to pick him up. However, the boy tries to hide his weaknesses from his father and, not wanting to make him worry, asks his mother not to tell him that he cried. Despite the frequent neglect from his father, Damian continues to admire him and tries in every possible way to meet his expectations, especially after the unexpected praise that he received from him after meeting Loid. Periodically, Damian also tries to get closer to his estranged brother, once approaching Demetrius to congratulate him on his academic achievements, and becomes somewhat upset that his attempts to have a casual chat were met with cold indifference.

Since Damian is still a child, most of his known abilities are limited.

Physical Ability: Although his strength as a child is limited, he is able to be one of the few that nearly survive to the end of the dodgeball match, despite having Bill Watkins as an opponent.

Endurance: Damian has shown to be quite tough, being able to block a shot from Bill Watkins, a kid who is much bigger than the size of an average 6-year-old.

Intelligence: As shown in his grades, Damian is a very studious and intelligent student, always striving for high grades and good scores. His discipline and responsibility made him have one of the highest grades in his class, and for this, he managed to get a Stella for being in the top 2 highest grades in the History midterm.

Desmond-Style Rolling Sweep
(デズモンド 流 ローリングスイープ,
Dezumondo-Ryū Rōringu Suīpu?) Damian's cleaning move, in which he spins forward in a circular motion while sweeping away anything in his path. Those nearby will get caught up in the dust clouds it creates.
Paradise Fist
(楽園の左手パラダイス・レフト,
Paradaisu Refuto?, lit. "Left Hand of Paradise") To deal with his buzzing feelings of jealousy toward Anya's new friends, Damian, with the help of Ewen and Emile, creates a "Paradise Fist" in his dream to acknowledge and make peace with his feelings. He later crafts a "physical manifestation" of the fist.

Lightning Note-Taking (ライトニング 筆記, Raitoningu Hikki?)
Imperial Scholar Cape Flap (インペリアル・スカラー ばさばさ, Inperiaru Sukarā Basabasa?)

Scoleciphobia: Damian is terrified of worms. He runs away in a panic from Ewen and Emile when they chase him, holding these invertebrates in their hands.

Insecurity: Behind his prideful behavior, Damian is actually very insecure about himself and has low self-esteem, mainly due to the estrangement between other family members. He secretly believes that his own family considers him a failure. Damian tries to hide it from others by acting arrogant and looking down on anyone who is beneath his social class.

Poor Vocabulary: Damian is stated to have poor vocabulary skills as his grade in Language Studies is very low. During his first term finals, he did not place in the top ten in the subject and was later assigned to Class F, a lower class, alongside Anya for the next term.

Damian scores a 94 on the History midterm, placing him in the second-highest score in his grade for the subject and earning him a Stella Star.
Because of his brave actions during the bus hijacking incident, Damian earns his second Stella Star alongside Anya, Becky, and Bill.
Damian earns his third Stella for getting the highest score in his grade for the History term finals.

(To himself): "I gotta be the MVP in this game so I can score a Star. I need to become an Imperial Scholar like my brother did. Otherwise... Dad won't pay any attention to me at all."
(To himself, referring to Donovan): "I know father couldn't care less about me. If I want to please him... If I want to earn his respect... I have to be perfect. I have to become an Imperial Scholar!"

entries.name: Sylvia Sherwood
entries.content:
“Stop waiting for easy answers to fall into your lap, rookie. Use that head of yours to find them for yourself.”
— Sylvia to a WISE Rookie

Sylvia Sherwood (シルヴィア・シャーウッド, Shiruvuia Shāuddo?), also known as Handler (管理官ハンドラー, Handorā ?) or the "Fullmetal Lady" (鋼鉄の淑女フルメタル・レディ, Furumetaru Redi?), is one of the recurring characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. She is the commanding officer of WISE within Ostania and Twilight's main contact for Operation Strix.

Sylvia is a tall woman with a slim figure and narrow blue eyes. She has wavy red hair reaching the middle of her back. She is also sometimes seen having pink nail polish.

Though Sylvia disguises herself in public, she typically sports a pair of round-framed glasses and a black, wide-brimmed hat with a dark pink band that has a bow on the side. In her role as "Handler," Sylvia most frequently wears a fitted black dress with a low-cut square neckline over a white collared shirt and a large black ribbon tied under the collar like a loose bow, as well as square-shaped drop earrings in the shape of WISE's symbol. The back of her dress is long, reaching below her knees, while the front reaches mid-thigh. She also wears fishnets over black stockings with black high heels.

Sylvia briefly wore garish rings that were gifted to her by Loid and Fiona as souvenir after the two won the Campbelldon tennis tournament for an infiltration mission.

Sylvia's age is unknown, but it is advanced enough to the point that it has become a concern for her in physical combat, and even Anya has commented on how old she looks.

As Secretary Sherwood, Sylvia ties her hair in a ponytail and dons rectangular-shaped glasses. She also wears a dark coat over a black suit and skirt.

Little has been revealed about Sylvia's personality. She is similar to Twilight in her commitment, skill, and logical approach to her endeavors. She is extremely dedicated to her given task; preserving peace between Westalis and Ostania by inserting Twilight into Donovan Desmond's inner circle. Like Twilight, she is willing to assist Anya's acquisition of Stella Stars by any means (including deception and espionage). Despite this, some of her plans for ensuring Operation Strix's success—such as bribing Anya or creating scenarios where Anya can be framed positively—have been dubious at best, and her suggestions for Operation Strix have posed unnecessary danger for the spies she manages. Dubbed the "Fullmetal Lady" by her agents, Sylvia has a fearsome reputation, as even her best agent, Twilight, would not even address the price tag she unknowingly left on her disguise out of fear and imagined that she would hold him at gunpoint to continue working if he asked for time off.

Sylvia is deeply compassionate and has a gentle and motherly side. Having been a mother herself, Sylvia said that she once had a daughter around Anya's age, who is implied to have been lost during the second East-West war. She demonstrates these strengths in allowing Anya to keep Bond after Minister Brantz's assassination attempt and placating the child's concerns about the welfare of the other bomb dogs. She also appears to have a soft spot for animals, as she took in one of the dogs as her own pet, naming him Aaron, who she bonds with and takes good care of.

As shown in her speech to the student terrorists, Sylvia has a deep-seated hatred of war. Her fervent disgust for—and knowledge of—the atrocities and horrors of war seem to indicate that she suffered a great deal in the last conflict.

While training rookie agents, Sylvia expresses a strong distaste for ignorance and instructs them to act based on objective reasoning. As such, she orders them to keep an open mind and to search for truths themselves, stressing the value of information. Though she can be hard on her agents, Sylvia does care for them and their health—though Sylvia herself has admitted that she cherishes her most valuable workers and had to get told off by upper management about overworking them to ease up. She has allowed Loid to take time off to go on a vacation with his family and after he collapsed in his own home, and told Fiona to not push herself too hard and get herself killed.

Despite maintaining an immaculate public appearance, Sylvia's home is a complete mess, and she even tends to leave garbage in her office. Sylvia herself is indifferent to her mess and ignores her friend's loud complaints about it, although his duration eventually irritates her. She became unconcerned about tidiness due to the loss of her family during the war, believing that cleanliness does not matter when alone. However, Sylvia later changes her mind for the sake of her dog, who begins to suffer due to the mess in their apartment. It is also established that her age is a sensitive topic for Sylvia, as she once became slightly offended by Anya, who told her "even at your age."

Sylvia has surprisingly a childish side that she rarely shows to others. When changing her disguise to avoid the two SSS agents tailing her, she actually admires the new coat she wore. While at a park with her dog, she immediately engages in a bet with Loid to see who has the best dog, wanting to prove her leadership skills are superior.
