A machine to make him taller. (Failed)
X-ray glasses. (Failed)
A pistol disguised as a toothbrush.

(To Fiona Frost): "Oh, I'm not on anyone's side. I'm just not a fan of the way the East does things. This country's too rigid. Too oppressive. So I like to shake things up with a little trouble sometimes. Guess I'm going through a rebellious phase."
(To Loid Forger): "I'm just saying, isn't it stupid? This whole war between East and West—it's all the result of a diplomatic fiasco. So why is it that all of us worthless peons gotta be the ones to clean up their mess? They tell us to hate each other. So we fight. And then we die. It's the most pointless thing in the world."

entries.name: Shopkeeper
entries.content:
“With proper watering and pruning… and careful maintenance… the world can remain a beautiful place.”
— The Shopkeeper to Yor Forger

The Shopkeeper (店てん長ちょう, Tenchō?) is the leader of Garden, the assassin organization in Ostania which Yor Forger is a part of. While he seeks to "keep this world a beautiful place," his motives are largely unknown.

The Shopkeeper appears to be a middle-aged man with tan skin, long and shaggy white hair that reaches down to the waist, and sunken almond-shaped black eyes. While working in his garden, he is shown wearing a brown hat with a red string that has two golden figurines in the shape of small spikes attached at the ends, which are similar to Yor's own earrings and weapons. The Shopkeeper also wears a beige long-sleeve shirt with rolled sleeves and pants alongside a black apron, gloves, and boots.

The Shopkeeper is a man who values the past and tradition of Ostania, seen by his devotion to the Miteran Empire, an old empire from the country's history. For example, he holds the Miteran elk in the former lands of the empire in high regard, respecting them as divine beings and asking his assassins to do the same. In contrast, the Shopkeeper has little interest in getting involved with political affairs, as he refuses jobs that appear politically motivated and declares that Garden only serves the nation rather than a politician.

The Shopkeeper is always seen maintaining his beautiful garden, tending to its plants and trees. The Shopkeeper seems to be a calm and patient person, often seen smiling calmly, and normally accepts any petition or favor Yor asks him. He also shows a somewhat mischievous side, swiping at Yor with his shears, seemingly out of a mixture of amusement and testing her awareness. The Shopkeeper has also shown mysterious moments, such as when he remained silent upon seeing Yor worrying about her family after giving her a new assignment and being intrigued when she later tells him about Loid's interest in Donovan Desmond.

While he is largely a mysterious man, his greatest ambition is to ensure the world remains a beautiful place, which he passes on to his assassins, particularly to Yor, whom he seems to trust deeply because he personally trained her. According to Yor, the Shopkeeper says that being an assassin is "a noble calling" and that his employees "should be proud as any soldier who has devoted their life to their homeland."

The Shopkeeper has known Yor since her youth, having taught her survival skills and trained her to be an assassin. When assigning Yor with assassin contracts, the Shopkeeper provides her with photos of her target, as well as information about their capabilities and defenses. The targets are given to the "Thorn Princess" because they are traitors to the nation of Ostania, whom he believes must be eliminated.

Not much is known about the Shopkeeper himself, but he has connections to the Ostanian underworld, as he states that he owed a personal debt to the former head of the Gretcher family before his death.

The Shopkeeper calls Yor to assign her a new job, but she mistakes him for her brother, Yuri; her tone makes him wonder if the siblings are having a fight, and he finds it unusual. After Yor apologizes for the confusion, the Shopkeeper moves on to inform "Thorn Princess" about a client at the Royal Hotel, Room Number 1307.

Later, after Yor gets married to Loid Forger and moves to the Forger residence to help with her cover identity, she recalls to herself that she was able to get the Shopkeeper's permission for this decision.

When Yor's daughter, Anya, picks her for a job investigation as part of her school project, Yor begins to imagine a scenario in which she explains her assassin job to Anya. She mentions the Shopkeeper, sharing his beliefs about being an assassin, and receives a call from him about a new client.

Yor is assigned to eliminate a faction of the Red Circus group in the northern district of Berlint. After completing her task, she calls the Shopkeeper to inform him of her mission's completion. During the call, Yor reports that she will be going straight home afterward but remembers that she promised Loid that she would pick up eggs and milk on the way. As she finishes their call, Yor fails to notice a surviving member who ends up shooting her butt, causing her great pain for several days.

The Shopkeeper informs Yor's manager, Matthew McMahon, to tell her that she has a phone call while they are working at Berlint City Hall. Yor goes to a private room in the building where she answers the phone, and the Shopkeeper greets the Thorn Princess and says she has a new "client."

The Thorn Princess and Matthew arrive at a garden maintained by the Shopkeeper. Yor compliments the garden, and he replies that with proper watering and careful maintenance, the world can remain a beautiful place. While Yor takes a moment to smell the flowers, the Shopkeeper decides to test her instincts with a surprise attack. After Yor successfully dodges it, the Shopkeeper apologizes for his sudden actions, saying it was to test her. Satisfied that Yor's skills have not dulled, he proceeds to brief her on her latest assignment, the protection of Olka Gretcher and her child, Gram, aboard the cruise ship Princess Lorelei.

The Shopkeeper briefs Yor on what the assignment entails, including its background and his personal connection to it. He watches Yor as she hesitates to take on the job because of her worries about making an excuse for her cover job and family. He informs her that Matthew has already prepared a cover story of her being there as part of her work, which puts her mind at rest. The Shopkeeper then entrusts the assignment to the Thorn Princess, who gladly accepts.

Yor visits the Shopkeeper to inform him of her meeting with Melinda Desmond, who wishes to be friends with her. Because Melinda is an important person in the country, she asks for his permission. The Shopkeeper says he has no problem with it but tells Yor that because Melinda is a conservative, he would not recommend it if "anything" were to happen. He then instructs Yor to at least watch herself to prevent Loid from thinking she has one-sided political beliefs. Yor says it should not be a problem, bringing up how Loid met Donovan Desmond and his interest in the National Unity Party, which piques the Shopkeeper's attention.

While going out for dinner with her city hall co-workers, Yor gets drunk and imagines approaching the Shopkeeper to request permission to kill Loid in order to maintain her cover as a normal housewife. The Shopkeeper approves, and Yor soon finds herself facing off against Loid and getting into a bloody fight with him. However, she quickly snaps out of her fantasy and tells herself that the Shopkeeper would never give her permission like that.

The Shopkeeper is visited by Director Wilker of the SSS at his mansion. After attempting to make some small talk, Wilker presents the Shopkeeper with a briefcase filled with files for job requests, mostly from Ostania's prime minister. The Shopkeeper turns the first two down due to them having political agendas until he reads the third file, a poaching case on Miteran elk in southwest Ostania. He accepts the job, explaining to Wilker the historical significance of the land's forests and how a portion is a demilitarized zone that could cause friction between East and West. Wilker agrees with the Shopkeeper's choice and asks him to consider the other files. However, the Shopkeeper rejects Wilker, sternly reminding him that Garden acts in service to the nation, not to a politician. The Shopkeeper then watches Wilker as he leaves the mansion with his men.

Later, the Shopkeeper meets with his assassins at his garden, interrupting a tense moment between Yor and Hemlock before starting their መeting. After Hemlock and Gympie complete their reports, the Shopkeeper introduces the group's new assignment to protect the elk by stopping the poachers, briefing them on its background and the potential risks they may face. Suspecting that their work will need to be divided over multiple missions, the Shopkeeper tasks Yor and Matthew with the first. Hemlock volunteers to join as support, which the Shopkeeper agrees with while requesting him not to harm the elk. Matthew plans to make arrangements at city hall in case their mission goes on for longer, a decision that the Shopkeeper supports.

Master Combatant: Although not much of his overall abilities have been showcased, the Shopkeeper appears to be an expert combatant. He uses a giant pair of garden shears as a weapon and has good control over them, as he tries to attack Yor with them with a quick and skillful thrust. He is also responsible for training Yor all she knows about being an assassin, indicating he is of comparable, if not a higher level of skill in the profession.

Teaching: The Shopkeeper has personally taught and trained Yor to become a full-fledged assassin. Upon meeting her again in person after she joined the Forger family, he tried to attack her while she was distracted to test her reflexes.

Gardening: The Shopkeeper owns a large garden where he carefully grows, cultivates, and maintains a wide variety of flowers and plants. Among them are grapes, which he uses to make vintage wine.

Similar to Loid and Sylvia in WISE, the Shopkeeper is Yor's mentor and handler in Garden, as he taught her survival skills in her youth and trained her to be the Thorn Princess and is mainly responsible for summoning and dispatching her to complete assignments. Despite allowing her to enter the Forger family as part of her cover, the Shopkeeper appears to have concerns about them negatively impacting her abilities as an assassin, such as when he tested her skills to see if it had been dulled by her family life and quietly watched her worry about her family after assigning her with an important mission.

In a rare instance, he assigned her a mission whereby she would protect someone, that being Olka Gretcher and her son. He also allowed Yor to become friends with Melinda Desmond, but gave her a warning due to Melinda's political alignment and that something could happen.

entries.name: Martha Marriott
entries.content:
“Madam... I know you think you have it all figured out. But understanding that you don't is the first step toward growing up.”
— Martha to Becky Blackbell

Martha Marriott (マーサ・マリオット , Māsa Mariotto?) is one of the supporting characters of the SPY x FAMILY series. She is a longtime servant of the Blackbell Family and typically acts as Becky's caretaker.

Martha is a fairly tall old lady with blue eyes and straight, gray hair styled in a low bun. She typically wears a black suit with a white undershirt, tied by a red bolo tie with a golden clasp in the shape of a bell with the letters "BB" on it, likely standing for Blackbell and representing her servitude toward the family. For jewelry, she wears two gold ball earrings.

In her youth, Martha had light brown hair. When she transferred to Eden Academy, Martha had a short bob that she grew out long enough over time to make two low braids. In her final year at the school, Martha had shoulder-length hair that she occasionally styled into a low ponytail.

After joining the military during the first East-West war, Martha cut her hair short. Over the months, when her hair grew a little longer, she cut it even shorter to disguise herself as a man during her journey from Westalis to Ostania.

Martha carries herself in a very dignified manner, not showing signs of anger when she is disappointed in someone. Despite working for a very wealthy family, she seems to show no care about class herself. In serious moments, she can become very strict and even protective over people she cares about, even scolding and reproaching them if they try something inappropriate or unexpected.

In her younger years, Martha was more impulsive and presumptuous. She got into fights with bullies and was not afraid to express her own opinion, even if it sounded too straightforward, which led to her quarrel with Henry Henderson, for whom she had unspoken romantic feelings. Martha also had a strong sense of patriotism and a desire to defend her country; however, due to the loss of her dream of becoming a ballerina, she also had a strong rage towards the West and was ready to fight even at the cost of her own life if it would allow her to take at least one enemy with her. But when Martha was faced with the care of an elderly Westalian woman, she slightly changed her mind about Westerners, realizing that there are kindhearted people among them too. Also, having been on the verge of death, she lost her zeal to fight with anyone and just wanted to return home to those she loved.

Fighting Skills: Being a former soldier that served in the two East-West wars, Martha has basic combat skills. However, unlike an average solider, Martha has notable high speed, once leaping into the air, shocking Vadim holding a captive Anya with a taser, and catching the little girl before she hit the ground in quick succession. During her youth, Martha was quite agile and was strong enough to fight three older students, taking down two using just her ballet techniques.

Dance Skills: In her youth, Martha was quite skilled in ballet—so much so that she used it to transfer to Eden Academy through a scholarship. At Eden, she focused on her ballet and entered the high school ballet program, even considering pursuing a ballet career. Martha was also able to use her ballet moves to fight three older students with great effect.

Special Moves
As a teenager, Martha used her ballet moves to fight three older boys at once while having the element of surprise.

Fouetté Kick
(フェッテキック,
Fette Kikku?) Martha performs a fouetté, a ballet move, quickly whipping her raised leg to kick her opponent.
Allongé Chop
(アロンジェチョップ,
Aronje Choppu?) Martha extends her arm and chops her opponent in the face.

(To Becky Blackbell): "Ah, you see, it's the things that we don't understand that make us feel uneasy. I'm sure that's due to some animal instinct deep within us. So we convince ourselves that we do understand things we don't, in order to make ourselves feel better. 'The people of that country are just plain evil.' Or 'It's the elites doing as they please again.' And maybe it is that simple. And maybe it isn't. But latching on to such assertions and persuading yourself of their truths—that's a certain sort of weakness. And a dangerous one. Accepting that you don't know is every bit as important as trying to learn the truth."

entries.name: Jeeves
entries.content:
“How I hope that these children are able to remain forever unbounded by the statures and standpoints of their parents, and continue seeking out their own happiness of their own accord. It may not be my place to hope for such things, but I cannot help but wish it all the same.”
— Jeeves about Damian Desmond and the other children

Jeeves (ジーブス, Jivuzu?) is a butler for the Desmond Family, typically serving as Damian's attendant.

Jeeves is a tall, handsome man with dark blue eyes and neatly styled black hair swept to the left side of his head. He is always seen dressed in a black tuxedo with a tie, consistently maintaining a formal appearance in the presence of the Desmond family.

Jeeves is a highly skilled and dependable butler, characterized by his commitment to the Desmond family. Despite his role as a servant, Jeeves exhibits remarkable initiative and resourcefulness, capable of adapting to any situation—whether preparing gourmet meals in the middle of a forest or using his quick reflexes to protect Damian from danger. His ability to stay calm under pressure, combined with his physical endurance and strength, makes him a formidable presence.

Jeeves also seems to have a close and communicative relationship with both Melinda and Damian, often discussing Damian's daily activities with Melinda and relying on her judgment for matters concerning the family, as seen when she personally selects cakes at her son's request, which Jeeves then delivers. While he maintains a professional distance, Jeeves's actions reveal a deep sense of loyalty and care for the Desmonds, particularly towards Damian, whom he constantly watches over and protects. Being aware of the estrangement between the Desmonds, Jeeves worries for Damian and knows he seeks a familial bond with them, so he often tries to cheer him up, even if it means lying to him about his parents.

Enhanced Physical Abilities: Jeeves appears to have basic combat skills and impressive reflexes, as demonstrated when he swiftly threw an acorn at a snake that was about to attack Damian, successfully immobilizing it. He also displays considerable endurance and strength, effortlessly carrying a heavy bag on his back for extended periods while constantly chasing after Damian to keep him safe.

Cooking: As a butler, Jeeves possesses exceptional cooking skills and is prepared to whip up any meal on demand. Even in the middle of a forest, Jeeves and the other butlers effortlessly unpack their cooking tools from their bags and prepare a gourmet dish for the children.

Jeeves normally serves under the instructions of Damian, whom he has nicknamed as "Master Dammy."[2] Being aware of the estrangement between the Desmonds, he tries to guide and cheer Damian, doing his best to make him believe Donovan is looking out for him and assuring him that Melinda, despite her absence, still cares about him. Jeeves also wishes for Damian to be unburdened by his family's reputation and able to find his own happiness in life, so he takes joy in seeing his young master acting like any other normal child would and being himself around his friends. Since Jeeves likes to satisfy Damian's childish desires, he has been called out by other butlers for coddling the boy too much.

On occasions, Jeeves accompanies Damian to places where he needs protection. When accompanying Damian, Jeeves often acts as a voice of reason to the boy and will try to dissuade him from immature acts. Aware of Damian's aspiration to one day become a politician and statesman like his father, Jeeves tries to instruct him on how to act as one, though his advice can be quite blunt as he calls the people he will have to rule over "those below" and "the common folk."

Although Jeeves and Melinda have not been shown interacting directly, it is evident that they communicate more frequently than he does with Donovan. Jeeves often discusses Damian's day with Melinda, including incidents like the day Anya punched Damian, much to the boy's annoyance. When Damian asks Jeeves for a favor, it seems Melinda is the one who often takes action, as in the case when Damian requested cakes for Anya, Jeeves mentioned that it was Melinda who personally selected the cakes, not him.

Almost nothing is known of their relationship, although it seems Jeeves has also served Demetrius, who, like Damian, has been nicknamed "Master Demmy" by him.[2] He is seen in the past accompanying him and Donovan during one of their study sessions.

Jeeves serves as the Desmonds' servant, including Donovan. Jeeves often reports to Donovan about how his sons are doing at Eden Academy, even mentioning to him the incident Damian had on the first day of school.

(To the other butlers): "I wonder... this area did draw a lot of interest during the treasure boom, but... well, it's not our place to tell them it's hopeless. Let's play along till they're satisfied, shall we?"[4]
(To Damian): "Worry not, Master Damian. I will lay down my own life if necessary to protect you."[5]

entries.name: Sigmund Authen
entries.content:
“You're a good girl. A fine child. Children like you are this nation's greatest treasure. Grow up healthy and strong.”
— Sigmund to Anya Forger

Sigmund Authen (ジークムント・オーセン, Jīkumunto Ōsen?) is an elderly man who is the husband of Barbara Authen and the Forger family's new neighbor. Yor and Anya help him get home after he gets lost in the city. He was a university lecturer during his prime, specializing in neurology but dabbled in cultural anthropology.

Sigmund is a short, elderly man with heavy wrinkles, being about a head taller than Anya. His hair is receding and messy, and he has a big, bushy beard and thick, drooping eyebrows alongside round-framed glasses with a high bridge.

Sigmund typically wears a cardigan over a V-neck sweater with a collared shirt underneath.

Despite his aging memory and being past his prime, Sigmund is still quite an intelligent man and can effectively teach others. Sigmund has a passion for learning, believing that it is one of the fundamental joys of being human, and he wishes to learn as much as he can. He shares this passion with those he teaches, as he shows them the importance of finding the joys of learning by making their lessons palatable to them in a way they can understand the material and also make it fun for them. Also, Sigmund does not skimp on praise when he sees the student's progress in their studies. During the lessons with Anya, he approves her progress with words or by tousling her hair affectionately, believing that she is doing a hard job.

It also seems Sigmund hopes for a peaceful future for Ostania after the wars. He has a soft side for children and believes that they are his nation's greatest treasure.

Sigmund is a highly regarded scholar and mainly worked in neurology. He also dabbled in other subjects like cultural anthropology and claims to have once toured the world to study local folk remedies as a fieldwork project. In his prime, Sigmund was a university professor and taught neurology and other subjects in Berlint, where he lived for a long time. At some point in his younger years, he married his wife, Barbara, and the two had a son.

Sigmund appears to have lived through both wars between the East and West. While walking through the district where his university is, he vividly remembers how the district was hit hard by the war and how the people reacted during those dark times. During the second war, Sigmund and Barbara went to Covenia, where Sigmund helped rehabilitate wounded soldiers. The couple eventually moved to the region for work, but when it came time to retire, they decided to return to Berlint to be closer to their son and his family.

Sigmund and Barbara move to 128 Park Avenue in the unit next to the Forger family. While moving in, Sigmund leaves to do some shopping and gets lost due to his poor memory. He is found by Yor and Anya, who try to help him find his way home. Their journey takes them through various parts of Berlint, including a marketplace, his old university district, and even a brief encounter with the mafia. Eventually, with the help of Bond and a raffle ticket, they arrive at the Authens' new apartment, where they are surprised to learn they are neighbors with the Forgers. Sigmund happily reunites with Barbara.

Later, the Authens invite the Forgers over for cookies. Learning of Anya's upcoming exams and her goal to excel in Classical Language, Sigmund offers to tutor her. He uses Anya's favorite comic, Spy Wars, as a textbook, making learning fun and engaging. His tutoring proves successful, as Anya earns a Stella Star for her performance in Classical Language. Sigmund congratulates her, emphasizing the value of learning the joy of hard work and its rewards.

Teaching: Due to his background in neurology and his exploration of other fields, Sigmund's experience in both academic and fieldwork settings gave him impressive teaching skills, having been a university professor. He later helps Anya study classical language, and thanks to his knowledge and interactive way of explaining the subject, Anya achieves a high score and is awarded a Stella.

Age: Due to his old age, Sigmund's memory is not very good. He is very forgetful, not being able to remember recent details such as the address of the home he recently moved into and tasks he planned to do for the day. However, Sigmund seems to remember his past a bit more, recalling his experiences in the wars quite vividly.

Barbara Authen: Barbara is Sigmund's wife. Sigmund greatly cherishes her, thinking of and missing her when he gets lost in their new neighborhood, even bringing her flowers as an apology when they reunite. Due to his poor memory, Sigmund often looks to Barbara for clarification or correction on past events or people's names. When they were younger, Sigmund used to be away from home all the time due to his work, though this did not appear to strain their relationship. The two are quite flirtatious, not minding to show off how affectionate they are in public. Sigmund and Barbara have a son together and have moved to Berlint to be closer to him and his family.

Anya Forger: Sigmund, nicknamed "Grandpa Siggy" by Anya, is the little girl's elderly neighbor. The two first meet when Sigmund gets lost in the park shortly after moving into 128 Park Avenue. As the Forgers try to help Sigmund get back home, Anya acts as his interpreter for Yor when he begins mumbling, though she often tends to misunderstand what he says. During their search, Sigmund is grateful that Anya does not make fun of him for his failings and begins seeing her as a granddaughter, doting on her as such.

Sigmund later becomes Anya's Classical Language tutor in preparation for her term finals. He teaches her the joy of studying, using her favorite series as their textbook, and does not forget to praise her for her progress. Sigmund later asks Anya what her ultimate goal is after her school achievements, and she answers "world peace," which greatly satisfies him. After Anya earns a Stella Star from her Classical Language grades, Sigmund and Barbara sincerely congratulate the young girl. However, despite his good-natured attitude towards Anya, Sigmund also tends to be judgmental when he thinks that she says unacceptable things. For example, when Anya believes that Sigmund will give her a lot of money as part of his estate, he quickly denies saying such things to her.

(To Anya, about learning): "Oh, the world is full of things that are a mystery to me. That's what makes it so much fun! Learning things is one of the fundamental joys of being human. Grasping the world's wonders... discovering how to make and build things... understanding the past, the future, oneself, others... I simply wish to learn all I can!"
(To Anya): "And now you've learned the joy of being rewarded for hard work. That's a treasure greater than even a Stella. And one day you'll experience the frustration of realizing that hard work is not always rewarded. But learning that is a treasure as well."

entries.name: Westalian Intelligence
entries.content:
“You and your fellow agents do great deeds that never see the light of day. You are heroes without shadows. You'll earn no medals. Your name will never make it into the papers. But despite that... never forget that everyone else's day-to-day lives are possible because of your blood and sweat.”
— WISE to Twilight

Westalian Intelligence is an intelligence agency in Westalis devoted to keeping the peace between it and Ostania. Their main division is the Westalian Intelligence Services' Eastern-Focused Division <WISE> (西国情報局対東課ウェスタリス ジョーホーキョクタイヒガシカ, Wesutarisu Jōhōkyoku Taihigashika?) which "Twilight" works for.

Little is known about the organization besides its main goal to maintain the thin veneer of peace between Westalis and Ostania. Some time after the second East-West war, WISE was formed by the Westalian government. Most of what has currently been shown of WISE takes place in Ostania. Whether through espionage, sabotage, wiretapping, and possibly assassinations, the WISE agents work to keep up the peace between the nations by removing anything that could threaten it. As observed from their headquarters in Westalis, they seem to have wide surveillance of various places with their cutting-edge technology.

WISE has agents embedded throughout Ostania to identify and neutralize any threats that threaten to worsen relations with Westalis. This can range from recovering stolen antiquities from Westalis to stopping unlawful export restrictions. All agents are commanded by a handler, who briefs them on current and future assignments to prevent incidents and watches for signs of restlessness. Within Ostania, Sylvia Sherwood serves as the commanding officer of WISE.

Other tasks that agents also have are gathering intel on their enemies to use against them or confuse them with misinformation. The gathered intel is sent to WISE's headquarters in Westalis, where it is then processed. To gather more information from their enemies, WISE has moles planted in Ostanian intelligence bureaus, where they feed the West with information and secrets. Individuals that also help agents with obtaining intel are informants. Not all informants that work with WISE are strictly affiliated with the agency, with some like Franky Franklin taking a more neutral alignment.

Located across Ostania are WISE safe houses, with their headquarters being the Westalis Embassy in the capital city of Berlint. Inside the safe houses are intelligence agents that obtain data and information, which they submit to their handlers. Safe houses are always kept hidden, from underneath a photobooth to inside building interiors, and are often locked behind secret passcodes and facial recognition technology. There are also other places in Ostania that are secretly affiliated with WISE, like the pet shop Kemono Park in Berlint.

Due to a recent spy purge, implied to be the work of the mole Winston Wheeler, a large number of spies have been exposed and captured by Ostania's counter-intelligence agency, the State Security Service, with many of those captees being female agents. As a result, WISE's manpower in Ostania has become short-staffed while operations are damaged, leaving remaining agents like Twilight to take on many extra missions and getting overworked by Sylvia.

Meeting with other agents in public is a dangerous task, as doing so carries the risk of both agents being exposed and captured, which is why it is a policy for agents to avoid unnecessary contact. When they do have to make contact, agents use many methods to communicate intel, such as hand signs, Morse code, and lipreading. Intel and secret messages can even be hidden inside coins or on food sauce. In the event of an incident, secret codes are shared between agents. For example, "Code 1399" suggests a serious incident.

Another way to communicate information is through ciphers. The names of these ciphers are mostly animal-based, with the intended cipher to be used indicated by the sound the animal makes. For example, a cat's meow indicates the use of "C Cipher", and a frog's ribbit indicates "F Cipher." However, because of their similar sounds, it is possible to confuse "F Cipher" for "T Cipher," which stands for toad. In another instance, a cipher can be indicated by the repetition of the first syllable, this cipher being "P Cipher," which uses the "po" syllable.

Operation Strix
Following the suspicious death of a Westalian diplomat in Ostania, WISE's higher-ups turn their attention to the National Unity Party's chairman, Donovan Desmond, who they suspect is planning a war. To probe him for any seditious activity, they create Operation "Strix" and assign it to their best agent: Twilight.

entries.name: State Security Service
entries.content:
The State Security Service <SSS> (国家保安局こっかほあんきょく, Kokka Hoankyoku?) is a counterintelligence agency in Ostania established to maintain domestic order and which Yor's brother Yuri Briar is a member of.

Their primary objective includes hunting down spies and surveilling the public. Some tactics they use include violence, wiretapping, intimidation, and torture. Due to their reputation, they are widely feared by the public and called the Secret Police (秘密警察ひみつけいさつ, Himitsu Keisatsu?).

The organization works as secret police, much like agencies in totalitarian regimes. They view the Westalian Intelligence, journalists, and spies like "Twilight" as their greatest enemies. They are effective at surveilling and capturing enemies, as seen with Franklin Perkin being captured in a matter of days after becoming one of their targets. With the rise of spies in Ostania, citizens can have people they deem suspicious arrested by reporting them to the Secret Police.

Upon being arrested by the Secret Police, suspects will be subjected to torturous methods in order to reveal any information they might have. Afterward, some suspects are released but kept under close surveillance, blackmailed into becoming their informants, or, if unfortunate enough, will never be seen again.

Officers are typically scouted from other agencies and are expected to keep their membership in the organization a secret, even from their family members. Within the SSS are currently four known divisions from Divisions 1 to 4.

According to Loid, there are many members in the National Unity Party within the SSS and Ostania's Justice Department. The SSS also appears to have a working relationship with Garden, Ostania's secret assassin organization. However, knowledge of their existence is limited to certain people, particularly Director Wilker and other higher-ups. The SSS offers jobs to Garden by sending them directly to the Shopkeeper, the organization's leader. These jobs can be requests from themselves or political leaders like the prime minister. Although they work together, Garden seems to hold more power compared to the SSS, as they are interested in serving only Ostania and can freely turn down any requests the agency gives them.

The SSS are feared by the public for their work to maintain order within Ostania. When Biddy Squire was killed during a Red Circus protest that went violent, her father, Billy Squire, became marked by the SSS due to his relation to her and fled the country with the help of the Red Circus to escape them.

A year before the first phase of Operation Strix was put in motion, Director Wilker recruited Yuri Briar, who was working at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. When the other members questioned why Wilker brought such a young man into their ranks, he simply stated that he found Yuri "adorable" and "like a cute little puppy."

During a gossip session between the Berlint City Hall clerks, Camilla tells Yor Briar of an event in which a 30-year-old bachelorette was turned in by her neighbors for being "suspicious" when Yor's age and single status are brought up. Later that day, Yor gets a call from Yuri, who tells her that he might receive a job promotion, but he is unsure about accepting it as he worries that Yor will be left alone. This spurs Yor to find a partner to avoid these suspicions, ease Yuri's mind so he can accept his work promotion, and continue her contract-killing work for Garden.

The Secret Police get word of city hall employee Jim Hayward stealing files from the office and selling them. The Lieutenant and two fellow members arrest him at city hall under suspicion of espionage. When Jim tries to resist, they knock him unconscious and drag him to their headquarters for questioning. Despite beating and torturing Jim to get his confession, the man refuses to budge. At Wilker's request, Second Lieutenant Yuri Briar takes over the interrogation.

Yuri immediately reveals photos of Jim selling the documents (which he forgot to submit), which gets him to talk. Jim reveals that he knows nothing about his dealer, aside from that he was from the West, prompting Yuri to ask if Jim knows anything about the Westalian spy Twilight. The interrogation goes south when Jim triggers Yuri about being disloyal to his family, causing Yuri to beat the man and be late for his visit to the Forgers. On his way to the Forgers' apartment, Yuri gets suspicious of the nature behind Yor's marriage and declares to imprison her husband, Loid, if he harms her.

During Yuri's visit, Loid (secretly Twilight) discovers Yuri's true occupation as a member of the SSS after Yuri talks about his work trip, in which he perfectly recites a script from the manual that Ostanian Intelligence agents use for learning deception. Meanwhile, Yuri remains suspicious of Loid and almost threatens to have him executed before leaving. The next morning, Yuri arrives at headquarters and laments not placing bugs in the Forgers' apartment, but quickly retracts the thought after his thoughts run wild. The Lieutenant urges Yuri to get over his sister complex for Yor and focus on their job.

On the day of the East-West ministerial-level summit for peace talks, rumors of a plot to assassinate Westalis's Foreign Minister Brantz spread amongst the intelligence agencies, prompting the SSS to place the conspirators, a group of isolationist students from Berlint University, under their surveillance. As the SSS agents keep an eye on the group, they catch wind of a bomb in the clock tower in the city and investigate it. Meanwhile, Yuri and other agents are sent to Brantz's hotel as a part of a contingent from the Foreign Ministry to guard him while escorting him to the summit. Unbeknownst to them, Twilight swapped places with Brantz beforehand, leaving the real minister at the hotel. By the time the SSS realizes Twilight's deceit, they are left to deal with the aftermath of the assassination plot being foiled and the terrorist leader's arrest.

The SSS takes note of Sylvia Sherwood, a secretary at the Westalis Embassy, and has several agents regularly tail her to check for any suspicious activity. However, they gradually become relaxed by her seemingly mundane schedule, allowing the WISE handler to move freely around Berlint without them noticing.

The late Ostanian Colonel Erik Zacharis is said to possess the "Zacharis Dossier," a collection of intelligence rumored to "reignite the flames of war" with supposed contents being records of human experimentation performed by Ostania and evidence of P.O.W. massacres by Westalis. The SSS get their hands on intel that the key to finding the dossier is within the Lady in the Sun painting previously owned by Zacharis, as it is rumored to have a secret code. Seeking to obtain the painting and the dossier, the SSS contacts its current owner, Cavi Campbell, who happily relinquishes it to them. However, the actual painting was taken by WISE agents Twilight and Nightfall, who infiltrated Cavi's estate and swapped the original with a forgery that has no secret code shortly before the SSS agents arrived to collect it.

With the biannual Imperial Scholars mixer in session at Eden Academy, SSS officers go to the school as security for the event. In addition to the state-of-the-art detection devices and the nature of the venue, the mixer is impossible to be infiltrated by spies.

Sometime after the mixer, Yuri and the Lieutenant successfully bust an illicit dealing of MNG data and arrest everyone involved after closely surveilling them. Shortly afterward, Yuri is assigned by his superior to investigate Franklin Perkin, who has been writing books and articles being released in Westalis that mock and slander Ostania. Yuri is instructed to secure evidence of Franklin's crime and the identity of his publisher. After a week of surveilling Franklin, Yuri thoroughly completes his assignment and has him and his publisher arrested after catching Franklin sending his manuscript through his workplace at the post office.

However, during his investigation, Yuri ends up sympathizing with Franklin's desire to support his family through his work and decides to have Franklin arrested away from the eyes of his father, whom Yuri arranges to receive financial assistance. As he gets taken away, Franklin poses the question of who the true disgrace to their country is between him and Yuri, to which Yuri answers that he would never do anything to cause his family pain. Yuri is later approached by Wilker, who asks if the workload is stressing him, but Yuri assures him that this is the perfect job for him. Yuri visits the Forgers that night and is reassured by Yor's smile that he dutifully works to protect.

When the cruise ship Princess Lorelei takes off for a three-day, two-night trip, several SSS agents board the ship to monitor the many celebrities and political elites there. On the second night of the trip, the agents are informed by the crew that a bomb has been found in the ship's bilge. While some agents discuss evacuating the ship, others are at the bilge, pleading with the crew to disarm the bomb. A crew member reveals himself to be a former marine and bomb disposal technician (who is actually a disguised Twilight) and offers his help. Despite successfully disarming the bomb, Twilight surmises that there may be more bombs to sink the ship and suggests evacuating the passengers as a precaution. The lead agent rejects this, not wanting to cause panic among the guests and to save face within the organization. He then orders every free agent and the crew to scour the ship for more bombs, starting a covert mission to disarm all the bombs within the ship. After completing their task, Twilight requests that the agents stay on high alert for the remainder of the voyage.

The agents follow these orders and keep watch for any suspicious activity when Princess Lorelei arrives at the resort island on its third and final day. After the voyage, the SSS keeps the failed bombing incident on the ship hidden from the public. Surmising that the bomber's goal was to instigate more conflict between Ostania and Westalis, they suspect that a third country was involved. Despite the organization's suspicions, Sylvia believes that they will inevitably bury the incident to save face.

"The Quill" is a skilled counterfeiter in Berlint. However, his identity was exposed by the SSS in the past, forcing him to stay at home to avoid getting caught by them. One night, the SSS receives a tip that the counterfeiter left his home to visit a club and begin tailing him. When "The Quill" leaves the club, he is made aware of their presence and begins fleeing. The SSS agents attempt to capture him, but they are all defeated by Nightfall, who tipped the SSS as part of her scheme to get "The Quill" to gain her trust and accept her job request.

At headquarters, Wilker receives a report from Division 4 that the current leader of the remnants of the Red Circus, Billy Squire, is commanding a faction in Berlint. Shortly after, the Red Circus makes their move as they kidnap two school buses full of Eden Academy first-graders as hostages. One of the students, Becky Blackbell, has an S.O.S. note thrown out of her bus, which is discovered by passersby and reported to her family at the Blackbell Company. The Blackbells share the details of Becky's note with the SSS, who determine that the Red Circus is behind the kidnappings. The Lieutenant's superior officer orders that the suspects be oppressed and to cover up any information about the incident from the public.

The main bus hijacked by Billy Squire is stopped by the Berlint City Police, who attempt to negotiate with the Red Circus for the hostages' safety. An SSS captain and his squad arrive at the crime scene to take over the situation, intending to storm the bus immediately. The police commander is against it and states that they are under orders from the ministry to wait, much to the Captain's irritation. Yuri, whose niece Anya Forger is among the hostages, is forbidden from going by the Lieutenant to prevent being recognized. Yuri insists on going anyway, which leads to him getting tied to a pillar at headquarters. As the SSS tries to locate the second bus, they receive an anonymous tip that a bus possibly containing the other students was seen in the Demforest district. Yuri overhears this and convinces his fellow officers to let him investigate the lead since he has good informants in that area. With this lead, headquarters orders the Captain and his men to be on standby until "Bus B" is found. While they wait, snipers carefully watch the bus and also await orders.

While gathering information and scouring the district, Yuri finds Bus B stashed in a warehouse. After confirming the bus's location, Yuri calls a small team of SSS agents to raid the warehouse. The agents swiftly execute all of the Red Circus members inside and secure the hostages while unscathed, except Yuri, who is shot in the shoulder. With Bus B secured, the Captain is given command of the situation. The Captain proceeds to inform Billy's bus that their comrades are dead and gives them until dawn to surrender. After making his announcement, the Captain prepares a guard regiment to storm the bus at night, tired of playing games with the group.

To the surprise of everyone, Billy Squire steps out of the bus and surrenders. Billy's comrade Vadim makes a desperate attempt to flee with the bus but is stopped by the police's armored vehicles. When he exits the bus with Anya as his hostage, the Captain orders his men to shoot to kill, but Blackbell family servant Martha Marriott interrupts them by immobilizing Vadim with a taser, after which she rescues Anya. After the Red Circus members are arrested and the safety of all the hostages is confirmed, the Captain orders the information blackout to be lifted. Days after the hijacking, Eden Academy holds a parents' briefing, which does not go well as the SSS is also in attendance, and their presence stops the parents from speaking freely.

Winston Wheeler, an Ostanian Intelligence operative embedded in WISE HQ in Westalis as a mole, steals numerous top secret documents from their files before fleeing the agency. To ensure Winston is secured when he returns to Ostania, Wilker holds an emergency summons to order his subordinates to cooperate with Division 4 during this process and to not let WISE interfere. To avoid causing trouble with Westalis due to the stolen files, the government decides not to approve of the operation, forcing the agents to go undercover in Shellbury, where they are to meet with Winston at the local hotel.

The SSS informs Winston and the agents that their signal is a "green tie with a gemstone tiepin." To single out any moles in their ranks, they tell certain branches of their communications division a color for the tiepin but tell each agent a different color. While surveilling the streets, Yuri encounters what he believes to be Winston, who requests to change the meeting location to a park. At the park, "Winston" meets with Captain Gascoigne and his squad and states that their signal was a "green tie with a yellow gemstone tiepin" to confirm his identity. Gascoigne reports the color to Wilker, who quickly identifies Officer Jeffrey as the mole for WISE. The agents then expose the faux Winston as Twilight, who is also after the real Winston and the files.

The agents attempt to capture Twilight, but he evades them as he reveals hidden traps around the park. The agents seal off the park's exits but are once again duped by Twilight, who diverts them to the east gate while disguised as Yuri. Meanwhile, the real Yuri is with the Lieutenant and sees his footprint in an area that he has never stepped on. Seeing a sewer just ahead of the footprint, Yuri reports that Twilight may have gone to the sewers. Yuri insists on catching Twilight and descends to the sewers to chase after him while the Lieutenant sends backup to guard the sewer exits. In the sewers, Yuri finds Twilight disguised as him, leading to a fight when he tries to arrest him. Twilight wins the fight but is injured from a gunshot to his right arm by Yuri. He also leaves Yuri alive due to his connection with Yor.

On the surface, Winston is already at the hotel but is suspicious due to never receiving Gascoigne's signal. He then notices Gascoigne leaving the hotel and realizes that WISE has beaten them there. Wary of Gascoigne's movements, Winston shadows him in disguise. Unbeknownst to Winston, the Gascoigne he sees is actually a WISE Agent who seeks to lure him out and capture him. The WISE Agent calls his allies to stage a car accident to identify bystanders in the area who are agents. Winston notices the crash but keeps his eyes on "Gascoigne" by moving his eyes to the building across the street to watch him through the reflection of the windows. Nightfall notices this movement and immediately singles out Winston, who begins running upon realizing he has been caught.

Winston is eventually cornered by Nightfall and another agent, and they retrieve the files from him. As they prepare to have him taken in as he may have memorized its contents, Winston forces himself free and escapes into the sewers with Nightfall in pursuit. In the sewers, Winston finds Twilight and sees through his attempt to trick him. Determined to unmask Twilight, Winston defeats him in combat but is stopped by Nightfall, who overpowers and defeats him. On the other hand, Yuri is found by the Lieutenant and fellow agent Chloe, the latter returning him to the surface for treatment while the former attempts to go after Twilight. However, Twilight and the other WISE agents evade their detection and take the captured Winston to WISE.

While the operation to secure Winston failed, both agencies lost a mole, so the SSS decided to consider things a draw with WISE. Upon returning to Berlint, Yuri visits Yor at the Forger home. There, he sees that Loid has also been injured and shares a similar wound with Twilight after observing a slight twitch in his arm. Suspecting that Twilight could be someone close to him, Yuri confronts Loid and checks his arm, only to find nothing.

While the SSS searches for individuals matching Twilight's injury, Yuri's mood worsens as he laments his losses to Twilight and questions his ability to protect his sister. Yuri takes out his frustrations on suspect Bobby Bockle during an interrogation, which worries Chloe. Yuri and Chloe investigate the hideout of Bobby's anti-government group, the Chicken Circle, where Yuri takes down most of the members on his own. Chloe saves Yuri from the final member and literally slaps sense into him to make him realize that he should prove to Yor that he can protect himself. Yuri misunderstands that he must work on his defensive skills and begins to train, much to Chloe's confusion.

During the winter, the SSS begins cracking down on an information network within Berlint. They capture the informant Latchkey Lachy, who gives them a lead on a fellow informant, a racetrack teller. The officers raid the teller's home and manage to round up more informants from the network, detaining them in a truck. While trying to interrogate the teller, Franky Franklin appears to rescue him. Despite the SSS calling in reinforcements, Franky uses his quick wit, gadgets, and knowledge of the city to fight back against and escape the agents while freeing his fellow informants.

As springtime approaches, Yuri, Chloe, and the Lieutenant are busy interrogating a recent wave of prisoners at headquarters, much to the former's exhaustion. After work, Wilker invites the trio to have steak together to celebrate Yuri's fight with Twilight. Yuri declines, saying he has a date tonight, shocking Chloe, though the Lieutenant correctly guesses it will be with Yor. Later that night, the SSS officers go drinking at a bar. After Wilker leaves, the Lieutenant calls Yuri, who just returned home from his hangout with Yor, to invite him out for bar hopping with their fellow officers. He also jokes that Chloe misses him, which she denies in embarrassment. Yuri accepts the offer and prepares to meet with his co-workers at their usual meeting spot.

Wilker, accompanied by other officers, drives out to a mansion in the forest to meet with the Shopkeeper. When two officers protest after they are kept from accompanying Wilker to his meeting, he orders them to stand down as the members of Garden could kill them. After attempting to chat with the Shopkeeper, Wilker presents him with a briefcase filled with files for job requests, mostly from Ostania's prime minister. The first two files disinterest the Shopkeeper as they have political agendas. However, he accepts a job to stop poachers from hunting Miteran elk in the southwest forests of Ostania, explaining the historical significance of those lands and how it is a demilitarized zone that could cause friction between East and West. Wilker asks him to consider the other files, but the Shopkeeper rejects him, reminding him that Garden acts in service to the nation, not to a politician. While leaving the mansion with his men, Wilker scoffs at the Shopkeeper, saying that his loyalty is to a dead empire.

The standard uniform of the SSS consists of a dark green peaked visor cap with a glossed black visor, a collared white shirt with a black tie under a dark green jacket, which is fastened with a black belt, dark green pants, and black gloves and boots. The symbol of the SSS is seen as a badge on the cap, while the jackets have marks on their shoulders and notch lapels that indicate their rank. Members also appear to be allowed to wear additional accessories, such as sunglasses and earrings. Members of lower ranks wear dark green side caps that also have the SSS symbol as their cap badge.

The Guard Regiment officers that are introduced in the Red Circus Arc appear to wear camouflage uniforms along with a simple ballistic vest and a belt with several utility pouches. They use titanium helmets and possibly wear balaclavas under them. They are mainly armed with rifles but are also seen with axes, sledgehammers, and ladders, presumably for operations that require breaching buildings or vehicles.

On the lapels of the jackets, there are insignia marks that indicate a member's rank. The marks of higher-ranking officers like Wilker and the SSS Superior are yellow with a red stripe in the middle. The marks of lieutenants like Yuri and his captain are red with a yellow stripe in the middle. Some marks have black and white circles that further indicate their rank, with three circles appearing to represent the higher ranks. Lower-ranking members appear to have all-red marks.

entries.name: Garden
entries.content:
“We at Garden act in service of the nation. We have no intentions of becoming the peons of some politician.”
— The Shopkeeper to Wilker

The Garden Assassins Syndicate (暗殺組織「ガーデン」, Ansatsu Soshiki Gāden?), simply known as Garden, is a secret assassin group that operates within Ostania, with Yor Forger being a prominent member known as "Thorn Princess."

Garden is an unofficial paramilitary organization led by the mysterious Shopkeeper, who appears to be devoted to the history of the Miteran Empire. Their primary mission is to "make the world a beautiful place" by eliminating individuals deemed "traitors" to Ostania. Their existence is largely unknown to the public, often considered an urban legend, but a few higher-ups in the State Security Service (SSS) are aware of them.

Garden maintains connections with the Ostanian underworld and has a working relationship with the SSS. However, they position themselves above political influence, acting solely in service of the nation and retaining the authority to refuse missions from the SSS if they do not align with their interests.

Assassination missions, termed "pruning," are assigned by the Shopkeeper, typically via phone call or in person at his private garden. These missions target groups or individuals identified as threats to Ostania. Garden provides their assassins, referred to as "pruners," with intelligence reports on their targets, and managers like Matthew McMahon assist in creating cover stories and alibis. In rare instances, dictated by the Shopkeeper's interests (such as his personal debt to the former Gretcher family head), missions may involve protecting clients instead of eliminating them.

The assassins of Garden are highly skilled and consider their profession a noble calling, akin to soldiers serving their homeland. The organization is estimated to have at least 11 members, possibly more. High-ranking members like Matthew McMahon appear to oversee the "pruners." Garden assassins possess exceptional combat abilities, expertise in stealth, sharp senses, high accuracy, and proficiency in cleaning up bloody scenes to leave no trace. Both Thorn Princess (Yor) and Matthew are portrayed as significantly more capable than other assassins outside their organization.

For certain missions, particularly in environments like forests, Garden provides a specialized uniform consisting of a beret, a buttoned jacket with 'Garden' nametape and a plant insignia, pockets, a buckle belt, and black boots. Assassins can customize this uniform with additions like weapon sheaths or utility pouches.

entries.name: National Unity Party
entries.content:
The National Unity Party (国家統一党こっかとういつとう, Kokkatōitsutō?) is a major political party in Ostania led by Donovan Desmond. They are influential enough to threaten the peace between the East and West.

The National Unity Party is described as a far-right-wing political party in Ostania. They formerly ruled the nation with a strong anti-Westalis notion up until the end of the second East-West war, when they fell out of power and became the opposition party for over a decade. In the present, WISE suspects that the party's current chairman, Donovan Desmond, is planning another war against Westalis, so they put Operation Strix into motion to investigate him and prevent this potential war.

The National Unity Party ruled Ostania during the second East-West war. When the war began, Chapman was the party's chairman and the Prime Minister at the time. Some time during the war, he was succeeded by Donovan Desmond. While in power, the party openly shared their anti-West values with the public and used tabloids like the Weekly Unify as mouthpieces for their political views. However, toward the end of the war, the National Unity Party fell out of power and was replaced by a less hawkish administration that seemingly seeks to reconcile with Westalis in the present.

Despite losing power and Donovan becoming a recluse shortly after, the National Unity Party remains active, holding seminars and other political activities while Donovan continues his work as their chairman. On the other hand, his wife Melinda, who was active in the party at the time, stopped involving herself in politics after they lost power. She currently serves as the chairwoman of the Lady Patriots Society.

During their rule, the National Unity Party led a research project known as Project Apple, which involved the creation of highly intelligent animals for military purposes by conducting experiments on them. However, the project did not produce any successful results, and it was quickly shut down by the new administration after the National Unity Party fell out of power. Despite the project being shut down, WISE has learned of rumors that some of its research teams may still be active in the present. It is currently unknown if these teams are somehow connected to Donovan through the National Unity Party.

Over a decade after the second war's end, the National Unity Party still holds its anti-West sentiments. When a Westalian diplomat is killed in a car accident while in Ostania, WISE suspects it was an assassination carried out by the party, whom they also believe is planning another war against Westalis, spurring them to create Operation Strix and assign it to their best agent, Twilight.

After Operation Strix's initiation, Twilight meets with Donovan during the Imperial Scholars mixer at Eden Academy, where he internally reveals that Donovan, and by extension the National Unity Party, seeks to control other nations with threats of military force.

Sometime after the mixer, Ostanian opera singer Jonas Wellman plans to visit Westalis for a cultural exchange event, which people hope will improve the relationship between the two countries. However, shortly before his departure, compromising scandals surrounding Jonas are published by the Weekly Unify and other Ostanian tabloids, which cause the singer to lose favor with the public. As the WISE agents in Ostania work to resolve the situation covertly, handler Sylvia Sherwood dismisses the authenticity of the tabloids and explains their history with the National Unity Party to a naive rookie. Days later, the scandals are rebutted by another paper, which has evidence that the scandals are part of a smear campaign against Jonas, including photos of one of his alleged mistresses meeting with an official from the party, implying that it was their handiwork.

According to Loid, there are many members in the party within the SSS and Ostania's Justice Department.
